docs.title: MerMEId MeLODy
docs.text:
MerMEId MeLODy is an open-source, browser-based metadata editor designed specifically for creating well-formed MEI (Music Encoding Initiative) metadata for thematic work and source catalogues. It is the successor to MerMEId, the established metadata editor for thematic work catalogues originally developed at the Danish Centre for Music Editing.

The editor produces complex RDF/Turtle output that directly cooperates with MEI structures to ensure standards-compliant metadata. The RDF data model is precisely aligned with the MEI Schema (v5.1) and the FRBR (Functional Requirements for Bibliographic Records) conceptual model, so all structured metadata can be reliably transformed into MEI/XML for use in MEI-based workflows, research infrastructure, and digital editions. It is designed for musicologists, music librarians, and developers who need to create structured, interoperable, and FAIR-compliant metadata for musical works, sources, persons or events.

MerMEId MeLODy is currently in beta. Functionality is complete enough for real cataloguing work, but the interface and data model may still change before a stable release. Feedback is very welcome at cdmd@adwmainz.de or as Github Issue.

Open the Live Editor Getting Started Guide View on GitHub

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
MerMEId MeLODy connects your browser directly to a Git repository on GitHub or GitLab where all data files live. You load the repository into the browser's private storage (Origin Private File System) via the GitHub or GitLab API, edit entities using automatically generated forms, and push changes back to the remote — all without leaving the browser tab.

Each entity (person, work, source, place, etc.) is stored as a separate .ttl file inside a typed subfolder using the MeLODy ontology, which is structurally aligned with MEI elements and FRBR hierarchies. The forms are generated on the fly from SHACL shape files shipped with the editor, combined with the index files of your data repository, ensuring that your data entry follows MEI-compatible structures. The data model is fully transparent and customisable — you can adjust which fields appear in forms while maintaining compliance with MEI output requirements.

To get started you need a data repository. The quickest way is to create one from the GitHub MerMEId MeLODy Template on GitHub or from the GitLab MerMEId MeLODy Template on GitLab RLP.

docs.title: Who Is It For?
docs.text:
• Musicologists creating or maintaining thematic catalogues of composers' works or sources
  • Music librarians who need to describe sources, editions, and manuscripts as Linked Open Data
  • Developers looking to extend or integrate a SHACL-driven RDF editor into a digital humanities workflow

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Browser-only — no installation, no backend server; everything runs in the browser
  • Git-backed storage — data is stored in a standard Git repository on GitHub or GitLab (gitlab.com or self-hosted instances); the editor talks directly to their APIs
  • Local folder mode — in Chromium-based browsers you can also work directly on a folder on your computer
  • Local search indexes — search and linked entity dropdowns use index files inside the repository, which the editor updates on every save
  • RDF/Turtle output — all metadata is stored as Linked Open Data, ready for SPARQL endpoints and LOD integration
  • MEI output — MEI entity snippets and full MEI work files
  • SHACL-driven forms — data entry forms are generated automatically from SHACL shapes through the shacl-forms webcomponent of the ULB Darmstadt (in the MerMEId-specific version mermeid-shacl-form), making the data model easy to read, validate, and extend
  • FRBR + MEI-based data model — implements the MEI-compatible FRBR hierarchy (Work, Expression, Manifestation, Item) plus contextual entities (Persons, Places, Venues, Events, Performance events, Instrumentations, Bibliography, Letters); the MeLODy ontology structure mirrors both FRBR levels and MEI elements to ensure semantic precision
  • Cross-entity linking — link entities to each other, preview linked records in a floating side panel and explore related entities in the graph view
  • Multilingual interface — the user interface and the forms are available in English and German
  • No build step — the source code is plain HTML and JavaScript

docs.title: Beta Status
docs.text:
MerMEId MeLODy is beta software (version 0.9, released 2026-10-26). It is actively used in ongoing cataloguing projects, but you should:

  • Back up your data repository regularly (it is a standard Git repository — cloning it elsewhere is sufficient)
  • Expect occasional breaking changes between versions
  • Report issues or unexpected behaviour on GitHub Issues or by email to cdmd@adwmainz.de

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: This page gives a brief overview of planned and in-progress features for MerMEId MeLODy. The roadmap is maintained on GitHub Discussions and GitHub Issues — those are the best places to follow progress, vote on priorities, or suggest new features.

docs.title: Import
docs.text:
Import from MEI/XML

  • The MEI2RDF tool enables conversion of existing MerMEId MEI (MEI 4.0) XML catalogues into the RDF/Turtle format used by MerMEId MeLODy.

  • The tool uses a three-phase conversion process:

    1. Detection and deduplication of entities from MEI documents
    2. Enrichment of MEI files with entity IRIs
    3. Generation of RDF triples organized by entity type

  • Supports both GUI and CLI modes with configurable entity schemas and mappings, making it practical for projects migrating from the original MerMEId to the new RDF-based system

  • Currently in development and not yet publicly accessible, but will be available for open use in the future.

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
Export to MEI/XML and HTML

  • The RDF Template Engine enables transformation of RDF/Turtle data into multiple structured output formats. The engine is built on a flexible pipeline architecture using SPARQL queries and Jinja2 templates. It extracts data from RDF graphs using customizable SPARQL queries, constructs context objects with hierarchical entity relationships (Works → Expressions → Manifestations → Items), and renders them through modular Jinja2 templates.
  • The engine will support three output modes: individual entities, complete files with related resources, and register listings of all entities of a type. Outputs can be generated in MEI (Music Encoding Initiative) XML format for use in the original MerMEId or other tools, HTML catalogues for web publication, or TEI (Text Encoding Initiative) XML for some entities like persons and places. The system is extensible with custom SPARQL queries for entity extraction and custom templates for output generation. The tool can run locally via CLI for batch processing or be integrated into CI/CD pipelines via the static-publishing-backend Docker container for automated publishing
  • Currently in development and not yet publicly accessible, but will be available for open use in the future.
  • Future versions may also support additional export formats such as CSV and other structured formats as needed by specific projects.

docs.title: Planned Features
docs.text:
• Import from other formats — importers for additional metadata formats (e.g. MARC, CSV, existing LOD datasets).
  • Language Selector in the editor to switch the languages of the field labels and descriptions
  • Multiple tabs to open more than one entity
  • Split panel for the three components (Filesystem manager, Entity Editor and Entity Renderer) to adjust the size of each panel.

docs.title: Data Model
docs.text:
MerMEId MeLODy uses a Linked Open Data model based on established musicological and bibliographic ontologies. All metadata is stored as RDF/Turtle files, one per entity, in a Git repository.

This section documents the conceptual and technical foundations of the data model.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
• Ontologies — the external vocabularies the data model is built on, and the MeLODy ontology
  • FRBR Hierarchy — the core bibliographic hierarchy: Work, Expression, Manifestation, Item
  • Entity Types — all 14 supported entity types with fields and repository structure

docs.title: At a Glance
docs.text:
The data model is centred on the FRBR hierarchy as formalised in LRMoo and directly aligned with the MEI (Music Encoding Initiative) XML Schema (v5.1). The RDF structure is specifically designed to map seamlessly to MEI elements, ensuring that complex thematic work and source catalogue metadata can be reliably transformed into well-formed MEI/XML. Extended with contextual entities for persons, places, events, and bibliographic references, the model ensures both semantic precision and MEI standards compliance.

Work                     ← abstract creative work
 └── Expression          ← a specific realisation (score, arrangement, version)
      └── Manifestation  ← a published or distributed edition
           └── Item      ← a single physical or digital copy

Person  Place  Venue  Institution  PerformanceEvent  Event  Instrumentation  Bibliography  Letter

DataCatalog              ← one per repository, describes the catalogue as a whole
 └── DataCollection      ← groups Works / Manifestations into a work or source catalogue

All entity classes are defined in the MeLODy ontology (melod: → https://lod.academy/melod/vocab/ontology#).

docs.title: Entity Types
docs.text: MerMEId MeLODy supports 14 entity types, plus one data catalog per repository. Each type corresponds to an RDF class in the melod: ontology, a dedicated folder in the data repository, and a SHACL shape file that defines its form fields.

docs.title: All Entity Types at a Glance
docs.text:
Entity Type Folder Class IRI Description Work works/ melod:Work Abstract intellectual or artistic creation Expression expressions/ melod:Expression A specific realisation of a work or source Manifestation manifestations/ melod:Manifestation A published or distributed version of an expression Item items/ melod:Item A single physical or digital copy Person persons/ melod:Person An individual relevant to the catalogue Institution institutions/ melod:Institution An organisation (publisher, archive, library) Place places/ melod:Place A geographic location Venue venues/ melod:Venue A specific performance venue PerformanceEvent performanceEvents/ melod:PerformanceEvent A documented performance Instrumentation instrumentations/ melod:Instrumentation A reusable scoring description Bibliography bibliography/ melod:Bibliography A bibliographic reference Event events/ melod:Event A general event (non-performance) Letter letters/ melod:Letter A letter or correspondence document DataCollection dataCollections/ melod:DataCollection A named collection (work or source catalogue) belonging to the data catalog

In addition, each repository contains exactly one data catalog (dataCatalogs/catalog.ttl, melod:DataCatalog), which is edited via the Catalog metadata button in the repository panel.

docs.title: Work
docs.text:
Class: melod:Work | Folder: works/

The abstract intellectual or artistic creation — the composer's intention, independent of any particular realisation, notation, or performance. See FRBR Hierarchy for details.

Key fields: title (primary and alternative), composer (linked Person), catalogue numbers (opus, BWV, TWV, etc.), genre, related works, linked expression, data collections (file collections with citation and publication information).

docs.title: Expression
docs.text:
Class: melod:Expression | Folder: expressions/

A specific realisation of a Work defined by its musical content. See FRBR Hierarchy for details.

Key fields: title of this realisation, scoring/instrumentation (linked Instrumentation or inline medium of performance), key, meter, date of composition, scoring overview, movements and sections, musical incipits (PAE format), performance events (linked PerformanceEvents), related expressions, completion status.

docs.title: Manifestation
docs.text:
Class: melod:Manifestation | Folder: manifestations/

A published or otherwise distributed embodiment of an Expression. See FRBR Hierarchy for details.

Key fields: title as on the manifestation, publisher, place and date of publication, plate number, physical description and title pages (for manifestation singleton), related manifestations, linked items, linked expression, data collections (file collections with citation and publication information).

docs.title: Item
docs.text:
Class: melod:Item | Folder: items/

A single physical or digital copy of a Manifestation. See FRBR Hierarchy for details.

Key fields: holding institution (linked Institution), shelfmark and former shelfmark, RISM identifier, provenance notes, physical condition, link to digitisation, related items.

docs.title: Person
docs.text:
Class: melod:Person | Folder: persons/

An individual relevant to the catalogue — composer, arranger, performer, editor, dedicatee, or any other biographical entity.

Fields:

Field RDF Property Notes Surname schema:familyName Required First name schema:givenName Alternate name schema:alternateName Alternative names or spellings Link owl:sameAs GND, VIAF, Wikidata, etc. Must be a full HTTP(S) URL Gender schema:gender Allowed values: female, male, diverse Birth date schema:birthDate Single date (YYYY-MM-DD) or a date span Birth place schema:birthPlace Linked entity dropdown (Place) Death date schema:deathDate Same pattern as birth date Death place schema:deathPlace Linked entity dropdown (Place) Occupation schema:hasOccupation Description schema:description

docs.title: Institution
docs.text:
Class: melod:Institution | Folder: institutions/

An organisation relevant to the catalogue — publisher, library, archive, research institution, or performing organisation.

Key fields: name, abbreviated name, RISM siglum, place (linked Place), address, founding date, external authority link (owl:sameAs), description.

docs.title: Place
docs.text:
Class: melod:Place | Folder: places/

A geographic location — city, region, country — used as a reference point for persons, events, performances, institutions, expressions and venues.

Key fields: name, country, Link/SameAs (Geonames, GND, Wikidata, ...), description.

docs.title: Venue
docs.text:
Class: melod:Venue | Folder: venues/

A specific performance venue such as a concert hall, opera house, or church. More specific than Place — a Venue is located in a Place.

Key fields: name, place (linked Place), description, external link.

docs.title: PerformanceEvent
docs.text:
Class: melod:PerformanceEvent | Folder: performanceEvents/

A documented performance of a Expression. Links together performers, venues, dates, and the performed expression.

Key fields: date of performance (single date or date span), venue (linked Venue), contributors (linked Persons or Institutions with role and certainty), description, evidence of the performance (linked Bibliography).

docs.title: Instrumentation
docs.text:
Class: melod:Instrumentation | Folder: instrumentations/

A reusable scoring description that can be referenced by multiple Expressions. Defines the medium of performance (instruments, voices, ensemble type) independently of any specific work version.

Key fields: label (e.g. orchestra or SATB), medium of performance entries (instrument or voice type, count, solo or ad libitum, link to identifier), ensemble as part of a instrumentation (linked Instrumentation).

docs.title: Bibliography
docs.text:
Class: melod:Bibliography | Folder: bibliography/

A bibliographic reference to secondary literature — a book, journal article, chapter, or edition — that can be cited from Work, Expression, or other entity records.

Key fields: reference type (letter, article, book, website), author(s) (linked Person or Institution), editors, title in different levels, year, publisher / journal, volume/issue/pages, identifier (DOI, ISBN, etc.), link (to Zotero).

docs.title: Event
docs.text:
Class: melod:Event | Folder: events/

A general event entity for non-performance contexts — a conference, workshop, commissioning event, or premiere of a work without full performance documentation.

Key fields: name of the event, date (single date or date span), place (linked Place), description, contributors (linked Persons or Institutions with roles), evidence of the event (linked Bibliography).

docs.title: Letter
docs.text:
Class: melod:Letter | Folder: letters/

A letter or correspondence document. Used to document primary source material such as composers' letters that relate to specific works or expressions.

Key fields: title of the letter, sent and received (each with participant (linked Person), place (linked Place) and date), repository (linked Institution), shelfmark and former shelfmark, description. Letters are modelled with the correspSearch vocabulary.

docs.title: DataCollection
docs.text:
Class: melod:DataCollection | Folder: dataCollections/

A named collection of works or manifestations, e.g. a work catalogue or a source catalogue, belonging to the data catalog of the repository. The default collections dataCollections/works.ttl ("All works") and dataCollections/manifestations.ttl ("All manifestations") are created automatically; new works and manifestations are added to them.

Key fields: name, data catalog, type (work catalog or source catalog), restrictions of use, status (draft, candidate, approved, published), responsible.

docs.title: DataCatalog
docs.text:
Class: melod:DataCatalog | File: dataCatalogs/catalog.ttl

The data catalog describes the catalogue of the repository as a whole. There is exactly one per repository; it is created automatically and edited via the Catalog metadata button.

Key fields: name, contributors with roles (data manager, data contributor, editor, contributor, publisher), application ("MerMEId MeLODy"), description.

docs.title: Repository Folder Structure
docs.text:
All entity folders are present in a data repository created from the MerMEId MeLODy Template. In this Template you can find example .ttl files as well. The structure looks like this:

my-catalogue/
├── configuration/
│   └── config.json
├── dataCatalogs/
│   └── catalog.ttl
├── dataCollections/
├── works/
├── expressions/
├── manifestations/
├── items/
├── persons/
├── institutions/
├── places/
├── venues/
├── performanceEvents/
├── instrumentations/
├── bibliography/
├── events/
├── letters/
├── indexes/                
└── modules/
    └── datasets-generator/

The GitHub template additionally contains the workflows in .github/workflows/ and the data validation (package.json, tests/); the GitLab template contains a .gitlab-ci.yml. Folders for entity types without examples (e.g. events/, letters/) may be missing in the template — they are created when the first entity of that type is saved.

The folder names are defined in the configuration of the editor. Do not rename these folders.

docs.title: FRBR Hierarchy
docs.text:
The core of the MerMEId MeLODy data model follows the FRBR (Functional Requirements for Bibliographic Records) hierarchy, as formalised in LRMoo. This hierarchy separates a musical work into four conceptually distinct levels.

Work
 └── Expression         (a specific realisation of the work)
      └── Manifestation  (a published or distributed version of the expression)
           └── Item      (a single physical or digital copy)

Understanding this hierarchy is fundamental to working with MerMEId MeLODy, because it determines how entities relate to one another and which fields are appropriate at each level.

docs.title: Work
docs.text:
Class: melod:Work Folder: works/

A Work represents the abstract intellectual or artistic creation — the composer's intention, independent of any particular realisation, notation, or performance. A single work may give rise to many different expressions.

Example: Beethoven's Symphony No. 9 in D minor, Op. 125 is a Work. It exists as an abstract concept, identified by the composer's intention and the thematic catalogue entry — not tied to any specific score or recording.

Fields:

  • Title (primary and alternative titles)
  • Composer (linked Person as Contributor with role as Composer)
  • Catalogue numbers (opus number, thematic catalogue reference such as BWV, TWV, etc.)
  • Historic context of the work creation
  • Genre and sub-genre as classifications
  • Evidence as linked bibliography
  • Related works (part of a larger collection, preceded by, derived from, etc.)
  • Is realised in (linked Expression)
  • Data collections (automatically includes the repository's default collection "All works")

docs.title: Expression
docs.text:
Class: melod:Expression Folder: expressions/

An Expression is a specific realisation of a Work or a Source — a distinct version defined by its musical content: instrumentation, arrangement, language, number of movements, and so on. The same abstract Work can have multiple Expressions.

Example: An arrangement of Beethoven's 9th for piano solo is a different Expression from the full orchestral score. A revision by the composer that adds a new movement creates another Expression.

Fields:

  • Label of this realisation
  • Scoring/instrumentation (linked Instrumentation entity)
  • Movements and sections (can reference other Expressions as components)
  • Key, Meter, Tempo, mensuration and extent
  • Duration of the performed expression
  • Musical incipits (in PAE — Plaine and Easie Code — format or linked MEI)
  • Performance events (linked PerformanceEvents)
  • Related expressions (arrangements, translations, revisions)
  • Completion status

docs.title: Manifestation
docs.text:
Class: melod:Manifestation Folder: manifestations/

A Manifestation is a published or otherwise distributed embodiment of an Expression — an edition, print run, manuscript type, or digital publication. All copies produced from the same printing or distribution constitute one Manifestation.

Example: The first edition of the score published by Breitkopf & Härtel in 1826 is a Manifestation. A later critical edition by another publisher is a separate Manifestation of the same Expression.

Fields:

  • Title as it appears on the manifestation and link to identifier (RISM)
  • Publisher and place/date of publication
  • Physical description (dimensions, watermark, plate number, inscriptions) and formatted title pages (for manifestation singletons)
  • Classifications
  • Related manifestations (reprints, facsimile editions)
  • Embodies (Linked Expression)
  • Data collections (automatically includes the repository's default collection "All manifestations")

docs.title: Item
docs.text:
Class: melod:Item Folder: items/

An Item is a single physical or digital copy of a Manifestation — a specific exemplar held at a particular institution or location. Two copies of the same printed edition are two different Items.

Example: The copy of the 1826 Breitkopf & Härtel score held at the Staatsbibliothek Berlin, with shelfmark Mus.ms. 1234, is one Item.

Fields:

  • Label and link to identifier (RISM)
  • Holding institution/repository (linked Institution)
  • Shelfmark and former shelfmark
  • Provenance notes as events and date of acquisition
  • Physical description (dimensions, watermark, plate number, inscriptions, condition) and formatted title pages
  • Scribes (linked Persons and Medium description)
  • Link to digitisation (if available)
  • Classifications
  • Related items (components)
  • Is materialization of (linked Manifestation)

docs.title: How the Levels Relate
docs.text:
In practice, not every catalogue entry requires all four levels. A thematic catalogue might focus primarily on Works and Expressions, using Items only when documenting specific sources. The editor does not enforce a strict hierarchy — you can create an Item without a parent Manifestation, for example — but the relational fields in each form are designed to connect the levels.

Links between levels are stored as RDF property references between entity IRIs, for example:

<urn:uuid:works/2270604911> 
    a melod:Work;
    lrmoo:R3_is_realised_in <urn:uuid:expressions/2718778403>.

docs.title: Entity IRIs
docs.text: Every entity in MerMEId MeLODy has a unique IRI (Internationalized Resource Identifier) that serves as its persistent identifier throughout the dataset and in all RDF output.

docs.title: Default Format: urn:uuid:
docs.text:
By default, entity IRIs use the urn:uuid: scheme combined with the entity folder name and a random integer:

urn:uuid:<folder>/<IDprefix><randomInteger>

The IDprefix is optional and empty by default (see Repository Configuration).

Examples:

urn:uuid:persons/2847362910
urn:uuid:works/1031334055
urn:uuid:places/774035217
urn:uuid:expressions/9182736450

Each entity's IRI is also the name of its .ttl file in the repository:

persons/2847362910.ttl   →  IRI: urn:uuid:persons/2847362910
works/1031334055.ttl     →  IRI: urn:uuid:works/1031334055

docs.title: IRI Generation
docs.text:
New entity IRIs are generated using the Web Crypto API at entity creation time:

let array = new Uint32Array(1);
self.crypto.getRandomValues(array);
return array[0]; // a random 32-bit unsigned integer

This gives approximately 4 billion possible values per entity type. Collisions are statistically negligible for the scale of musicological catalogues.

docs.title: Fixed IRIs
docs.text:
Some IRIs are not random. Each repository has exactly one data catalog and two default data collections, which the editor creates automatically when a repository is selected:

urn:uuid:dataCatalogs/catalog
urn:uuid:dataCollections/works
urn:uuid:dataCollections/manifestations

The IRI is permanent: once an entity is created and committed to the repository, its IRI should not be changed. All other entities that reference it (via linked fields) store the IRI directly — changing it would break those references.

docs.title: Configurable Prefix: projectDomain
docs.text:
The IRI prefix can be changed from urn:uuid: to an HTTPS namespace by setting projectDomain in configuration/config.json:

{
  "projectDomain": "https://example.org/"
}

With this configuration, new entities receive IRIs like:

https://example.org/persons/2847362910
https://example.org/works/1031334055

docs.title: When to use a custom domain
docs.text:
• If you want your entities to have dereferenceable URIs — HTTP(S) URIs that resolve to a web page or RDF document when looked up
  • If your institution has a stable web presence and a namespace policy for Linked Data identifiers
  • For catalogues intended to be integrated into the broader LOD ecosystem (e.g. accessible from Wikidata or other knowledge graphs)

docs.title: Important caveat
docs.text: Changing projectDomain after entities have been created does not retroactively update existing IRIs. Existing entities keep their original urn:uuid: IRIs. Only newly created entities will use the new prefix. This means a mixed-prefix dataset is possible if the domain is changed mid-project — generally it is best to decide on the IRI scheme before creating any entities.

docs.title: IRIs in Turtle Output
docs.text:
Every Turtle file in the repository uses the entity's IRI as the subject of all statements:

@prefix melod:  <https://lod.academy/melod/vocab/ontology#> .
@prefix schema: <https://schema.org/> .
@prefix owl:    <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#> .

<urn:uuid:persons/2847362910>
    a melod:Person ;
    schema:familyName "Telemann" ;
    schema:givenName "Georg Philipp" ;
    owl:sameAs <http://d-nb.info/gnd/11862119X> .

Cross-references between entities also use IRIs directly:

<urn:uuid:works/9876543210>
    a melod:Work ;
    lrmoo:R3_is_realised_in <urn:uuid:expressions/1234567890> ;
    melod:hasContribution [
        melod:hasAgent <urn:uuid:persons/2847362910> ;
        melod:hasRole <…> # role term from the MeLODy vocabulary, e.g. composer
    ] .

docs.title: Linked Entities in the Forms
docs.text:
Linked entity fields in the SHACL shapes declare the index class of the target type, e.g. sh:class melod:PlaceEntity. When a form is opened, the editor appends all files from the repository's indexes/ folder to the SHACL shape, so shacl-form can offer every entity typed melod:PlaceEntity in the dropdown. The IRI of the selected entity is then stored in the Turtle file.

Earlier versions used a dataset: namespace in the shapes that was replaced at runtime with the datasetBaseUrl; this mechanism has been removed.

See Repository Configuration and SHACL Shapes for details.

docs.title: Ontologies
docs.text: MerMEId MeLODy does not define everything from scratch — it builds on well-established vocabularies from the cultural heritage and semantic web communities, with the MEI (Music Encoding Initiative) guidelines as the foundational reference for music-specific concepts. It adds a domain-specific ontology (MeLODy) that precisely mirrors MEI element structures to ensure that RDF metadata can be reliably transformed into standards-compliant MEI XML.

docs.title: External Ontologies
docs.text:
Ontology Prefix Used for LRMoo lrmoo: Core bibliographic hierarchy: Work, Expression, Manifestation, Item and their relationships CIDOC-CRM cidoc: Events, places, actors (persons and institutions as agents), temporal and spatial modelling Schema.org schema: Persons (name, birth/death dates and places, gender, external identifiers), organisations, basic descriptive metadata DoReMus mus: Music-specific extensions: instrumentation, medium of performance, musical keys, casting SKOS skos: Used in the generated index files: skos:prefLabel (display label), skos:altLabel (alternative labels), skos:broader (additional search context) and skos:related (links to related entities for the graph view) correspSearch cs: Letters: correspondence actions (sent, received), participants, places and dates DASH dash: Form widget hints in the SHACL shapes (e.g. dash:singleLine) OWL owl: owl:sameAs for linking to external authority records (GND, VIAF, Wikidata, GeoNames, etc.) MEI — Music notation and encoding concepts; XML output tab converts to MEI format for interoperability

Controlled vocabularies of the MeLODy data model (e.g. title types, roles, certainty) are published as melod-terms.ttl (prefix terms:) and imported by the SHACL shapes.

docs.title: The MeLODy Ontology
docs.text:
MerMEId MeLODy defines its own Music Metadata Ontology (melod:) for concepts not covered by the standard vocabularies above — in particular the entity classes used in the editor and properties specific to the musicological use case. The concepts are based on the MEI (Music Encoding Initiative) guidelines and are mostly linked to the corresponding MEI elements. It implements the FRBR (Functional Requirements for Bibliographic Records) conceptual model, organizing musical information into Work, Expression, Manifestation, and Item levels. MeLOD integrates established ontologies including Schema.org, LRMoo, CIDOC-CRM and DoReMus to provide a rich semantic framework for music metadata.

Ontology IRI: https://lod.academy/melod/vocab/ontology# Prefix: melod:

All entity types in the editor (Person, Place, Work, Expression, etc.) are subclasses or instances defined within this ontology. When you see a class or property prefixed with melod: in a Turtle file, it comes from here.

docs.title: Example: a Person entity in Turtle
docs.text:
@prefix melod:  <https://lod.academy/melod/vocab/ontology#> .
@prefix schema: <https://schema.org/> .
@prefix owl:    <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#> .
@prefix skos:   <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#> .

<urn:uuid:persons/2847362910>
    a melod:Person ;
    schema:familyName "Telemann" ;
    schema:givenName "Georg Philipp" ;
    schema:gender "male" ;
    owl:sameAs <http://d-nb.info/gnd/11862119X> .

docs.title: Developer Reference
docs.text: This section documents the technical architecture of MerMEId MeLODy for developers who want to understand, contribute to, or extend the editor.

docs.title: Sections

• Local Setup — how to run every part of the tool on your local machine
  • Architecture Overview — bootstrap sequence, technology stack, and module structure
  • Components & Events — detailed reference for each web component and the complete event map between them
  • Services — shared filesystem and index store services, credentials, storage, conflict detection
  • SHACL Shapes — how to define and extend form fields using SHACL

docs.title: At a Glance
docs.text:
MerMEId MeLODy is a static, browser-only MEI metadata editor — there is no backend server. All operations run entirely in the browser and produce RDF that is structurally aligned with MEI (Music Encoding Initiative) standards:

  • Repositories are stored in the browser's Origin Private File System (OPFS), or in a local folder opened via the File System Access API
  • Cloning, pulling and pushing go directly through the GitHub or GitLab REST/GraphQL APIs (modules/filesystem-manager/api-provider.js) — no CORS proxy is needed. isomorphic-git is used locally (repository config, staging, walking the working directory)
  • The UI is built with Lit web components and Shoelace
  • Forms are generated automatically from SHACL shapes by the shacl-form component, in the MerMEId fork mermeid-shacl-form
  • RDF data is queried via an in-browser Oxigraph SPARQL engine — also used to generate the search indexes directly in the browser
  • All dependencies are loaded from CDNs — no build step is required. An importmap in index.html maps the aliases #isomorphic-git, #isomorphic-git-http and #oxigraph; the same aliases are mapped for Node.js via "imports" in package.json, so the tests run the same modules.

Components communicate mostly exclusively through custom DOM events. There are no direct references between components, keeping the architecture loosely coupled and each component independently testable.

docs.title: Quick Start for Contributors
docs.text:
The editor is a static HTML/JS application — no build step is needed for most work. To run it locally:

git clone https://github.com/Music-Metadata-Tools/MerMEId-MeLODy.git
cd MerMEId-MeLODy
python3 -m http.server 8080

Then open http://localhost:8080.

If you have write access to the repository, create a branch directly (name it after the issue, e.g. issue-33).

If you are an external contributor, fork the repository first, then create a branch in your fork. Open a Pull Request against main of the original repository when ready.

Commit messages should be short and written in the imperative: "Add person converter", not "Added" or "Adding".

docs.title: Working with the SHACL Form Renderer Locally
docs.text:
The form renderer used by the editor is maintained in a separate repository: Music-Metadata-Tools/mermeid-shacl-form

It is a TypeScript/Vite project. To develop it locally and test it against a running editor, clone it as a sibling of MerMEId-MeLODy (i.e. both repositories must share the same parent directory):

# from the shared parent directory, e.g. ~/projects/
git clone https://github.com/Music-Metadata-Tools/mermeid-shacl-form.git
cd mermeid-shacl-form
git checkout development
npm install

Build the MerMEId-specific bundle:

npm run build-mermeid
# produces dist/form-mermeid.js

Start a single HTTP server from the shared parent directory so both repositories are served from the same origin:

# from the shared parent directory
python3 -m http.server 8080

Then update index.html in MerMEId-MeLODy to point to the local build using a root-relative path (avoids CORS issues regardless of whether you access the editor via localhost or an IP address):

<script type="module" src="/mermeid-shacl-form/dist/form-mermeid.js"></script>
<script type="module">
    import { registerPlugin, RichTextEditorPlugin } from '/mermeid-shacl-form/dist/form-mermeid.js'
    ...
</script>

Open the editor at http://localhost:8080/MerMEId-MeLODy/index.html (or the equivalent IP address).

Development cycle: edit files in mermeid-shacl-form/src/ → run npm run build-mermeid → reload the browser. No server restart needed.

Once your changes are ready, open a Pull Request against the development branch of the mermeid-shacl-form repository and revert the URLs in index.html back to the published path:

https://music-metadata-tools.github.io/mermeid-shacl-form/dist/form-mermeid.js

docs.title: Running the Tests
docs.text:
If you are working on core functionality (filesystem management, git operations), run the test suite:

npm install
npm test            # runs all tests with Vitest
npm run test:watch  # re-runs tests on file changes

Requires Node.js v22 or later.

To run only the unit tests (filesystem and RDF-XML converter):

npx vitest run tests/virtual-filesystem.test.js tests/rdf-xml-converter.unit.test.js

For integration tests (real clone/pull/push operations), you need a test repository and a GitHub personal access token. Create a repository from the MerMEId MeLODy Template and add a .env file in the project root:

GIT_TOKEN=<your GitHub personal access token>
GIT_USERNAME=<your GitHub username>
TEST_REPO_URL=<URL of your test repository>

Integration tests are automatically skipped if these variables are not set.

On GitHub, the Unit Tests workflow (.github/workflows/test-unit.yml) runs automatically for every pull request against main. The Integration Tests workflow (.github/workflows/test-integration.yml) is started manually by a maintainer (Actions → Integration Tests → Run workflow, with a branch or refs/pull/<n>/head as ref); it uses the repository secrets TEST_GITHUB_TOKEN, TEST_GITHUB_USERNAME and TEST_REPO_URL. The editor itself is deployed to GitHub Pages on every push to main (.github/workflows/pages.yml).

docs.title: Pull Request Review
docs.text:
PRs are merged into main by a maintainer once:

  • Unit tests pass (run automatically for all PRs)
  • At least one maintainer has approved
  • There are no requested changes or conflicts

We use squash and merge to keep the commit history clean.

docs.title: Application Architecture
docs.text:
MerMEId MeLODy is a static, browser-only application. There is no server-side component — all processing happens in the browser. The application is served as static HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files.

Browser
├── js/index.js                    ← orchestration layer (startup, language + event wiring)
├── modules/services/
│   ├── filesystem-service.js          ← singleton VirtualFilesystem shared by all components
│   └── index-store-service.js         ← shared Oxigraph store with all indexes/*.ttl (INDEXES list)
├── adwlm-filesystem-manager       ← left panel: repositories + staging area
│   ├── index.js                        ← adwlm-filesystem-manager component
│   ├── api-provider.js                 ← GitHub/GitLab REST + GraphQL provider (clone, pull, push, branches)
│   ├── constants.js                    ← shared constants (CORS proxy URL, scheme names)
│   ├── credentials-helper.js           ← token handling utilities
│   ├── oxigraph-node-adapter.js           ← #oxigraph shim for Node.js / Vitest
│   ├── add-repository-dialog/index.js  ← dialog for cloning a repository
│   ├── rename-filesystem-entry-dialog/ ← dialog for renaming repositories
│   ├── repository-settings-dialog/        ← dialog for changing username / personal access token
│   ├── catalog-metadata-dialog/           ← dialog for editing catalog metadata
│   ├── push-conflict-dialog/              ← dialog for resolving conflicts before sharing
│   └── virtual-filesystem/
│       ├── index.js                       ← VirtualFilesystem class (files, staging, push/pull, index generation)
│       ├── opfs-directory-filesystem.js   ← default storage (Origin Private File System)
│       └── fsa-directory-filesystem.js    ← fs adapter for local folders (File System Access API)
├── adwlm-entity-search            ← left panel: entity search
|   └── index.js                        ← adwlm-entity-search component
├── adwlm-entity-editor            ← main area: form editor
|   ├── index.js                        ← adwlm-entity-editor component and shacl-form renderer
│   └── entity-types-dialog/index.js    ← dialog for selecting a new entity type
├── adwlm-graph-view                   ← right panel: Graph tab
│   └── index.js                           ← adwlm-graph-view component
├── datasets-generator                 ← SPARQL CONSTRUCT queries, one per entity folder (index generation)
└── rdf-xml-converter              ← right panel: XML output
    ├── converters                     ← one converter module per entity type
    ├── templates                      ← MEI/XML output templates (one per entity type)
    └── types/index.js                  ← maps entity type IRIs to converter modules

Git hosts are reached through their REST/GraphQL APIs (api-provider.js). No data is processed server-side; the only external requests go to the Git host's API.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Each repository is a directory in the browser's Origin Private File System (OPFS), or a local folder opened via the File System Access API. Besides the data files and the .git/config (username, token, branch, remote, lazy-loading setting), the editor keeps some bookkeeping files per repository:

File Purpose .dirty.json Files that have been changed or deleted locally and not yet shared .snapshot.json The last synchronised content of locally changed files (baseline for unstaging and conflict detection) .remote-tree.json Manifest of the remote files for lazy loading (files are downloaded on first access)

docs.title: Bootstrap Sequence
docs.text:
When the page loads, the following sequence occurs:

  1. Shoelace ready — a script in index.html waits for Shoelace's tab components (sl-tab-group, sl-tab, sl-tab-panel) to be defined and then adds the class ready to the body. js/index.js itself starts by initialising Oxigraph.
  2. Fetch editor-default.ttl — the orchestration script fetches configuration/editor-default.ttl from the editor server. This Turtle file defines all registered entity types.
  3. SPARQL query via Oxigraph — the Turtle content is loaded into an in-browser Oxigraph triple store. A SPARQL SELECT query extracts the entity type definitions — type IRI, display label in the current UI language, folder name, SHACL file location. Types without a label in the current language are not returned.
  4. Pass definitions to the components — the extracted definitions are set as the entity_type_definitions property on adwlm-entity-editor, adwlm-filesystem-manager and adwlm-graph-view. The editor uses them to populate the "New entity" dialog and to load the correct SHACL shape for each file type; the filesystem manager uses the folder names to decide which folders are shown in the tree. The list of type IRIs is also exposed as globalThis.__MERMEID_ENTITY_TYPE_ALLOWLIST__ for the quick add feature of shacl-form.
  5. Components initialize — web components connect to the DOM, set up internal state, and register listeners for the custom DOM events they consume. The filesystem manager auto-selects the first repository and dispatches adwlm-filesystem-manager:repository-selected, which triggers loading the config and the search indexes.
  6. Output Panel wiring — js/index.js connects the Output Panel tabs (XML, RDF, Preview, Graph) to the entity editor. The output panel is updated when an entity is opened (adwlm-filesystem-manager:entity-to-edit) or saved (adwlm-entity-editor:entity-to-save), not on every change in the form.

docs.title: Language Switch
docs.text: window.__MERMEID_setUiLanguage(lang) (supported: en, de) is called by the language dropdown in the header. It reloads the entity type definitions in the new language, sets the data-ui-language attribute on all components and dispatches mermeid-ui-language-changed on window. Static texts in index.html are switched by showing or hiding elements with a lang attribute.

docs.title: Technology Stack
docs.text:
Library Version Purpose Lit latest Web component base class (LitElement) for all editor components Shoelace 2.17.1 UI components: sl-button, sl-tree, sl-dialog, sl-tab, etc. isomorphic-git 1.37.4 Local Git operations (init, config, staging, walking the working directory) OPFS / File System Access API browser Storage of repositories (own adapters in virtual-filesystem/) shacl-form mermeid-shacl-form fork SHACL-driven form renderer — generates HTML forms from SHACL shape files + quick add and rich text editor plugin Oxigraph 0.5.8 / 0.4.5 In-browser RDF triple store + SPARQL 1.1 engine. 0.5.8 (via #oxigraph) is used for index generation in the virtual filesystem; 0.4.5 is imported directly by js/index.js and the index store service (startup config loading, entity search, graph view) Vitest, memfs, dotenv dev dependencies Test suite

All dependencies are loaded directly from CDNs (cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com). No build step or package manager is required to run or develop the editor; npm is only needed to run the tests.

docs.title: Component Reference
docs.text:
MerMEId MeLODy consists of four web components, several dialog components, an orchestration script, a service layer and a converter module. The web components communicate mainly through custom DOM events, which keeps each component independently testable and replaceable.

Most events follow the naming convention <component-name>:<action> and are dispatched with bubbles: true and composed: true so they cross shadow DOM boundaries — either on the component itself or on document — and are listened to on document. Exceptions are entity-selected and mermeid-ui-language-changed, which use window.

docs.title: Orchestration Layer (js/index.js)
docs.text:
This is the top-level script that bootstraps the application. It is not a web component — it runs as a plain ES module loaded from index.html. Beyond startup (see Architecture), js/index.js is responsible for:

  • Entity type detection — when a file is opened, it looks for exactly one subject with a melod: type; otherwise an alert is shown
  • Language switch — window.__MERMEID_setUiLanguage(lang)
  • Passing data to the components — entity_to_edit (entity editor, graph view), entity_to_save (filesystem manager), entity_type_definitions, ui_language
  • Output Panel tabs:
    • XML tab — listens for serialised entity data and invokes the appropriate converter from modules/rdf-xml-converter/ to produce MEI/XML output
    • RDF tab — displays the raw Turtle from shacl-form.serialize()
    • Preview tab — renders the entity read-only in a second shacl-form in data-view mode
    • Graph tab — adwlm-graph-view

docs.title: Filesystem Manager
docs.text:
adwlm-filesystem-manager

File: modules/filesystem-manager/index.js

The left panel component. Manages the repository tree, the staged files queue, and all Git operations exposed to the user.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Display and navigate the repository tree (lazily loaded via sl-tree); only folders of registered entity types are shown
  • Clone, remove, rename, and synchronise repositories
  • Stage, unstage, and push (commit + push) modified files, with optional commit message and "Select all"
  • Check for conflicts before sharing and show the push conflict dialog
  • Highlight unsaved and unshared files in the tree using colour indicators
  • Load the selected .ttl file and dispatch it to the entity editor
  • Respond to save requests from the entity editor and update the index files in indexes/
  • Create dataCatalogs/catalog.ttl, dataCollections/works.ttl and dataCollections/manifestations.ttl if they are missing when a repository is selected
  • Open the repository settings and catalog metadata dialogs

docs.title: Repository Tree
docs.text:
The tree is lazily loaded. When a sl-tree-item[lazy] node is expanded, the sl-lazy-load event fires and _generate_folder_tree() reads the contents of that folder from the virtual filesystem. Each tree item carries its path in data-* attributes:

  • data-entry-type: repo-folder, folder, or file
  • data-entry-absolute-path: e.g. /my-catalogue/persons/12345.ttl
  • data-entry-relative-path: e.g. persons/12345.ttl

docs.title: Conflict Detection
docs.text: Before a push, VirtualFilesystem.checkPushConflicts() loads the current remote version of each file to be pushed and compares it with the version last synchronised locally (.snapshot.json). Files changed on both sides are shown in adwlm-push-conflict-dialog, which renders both versions with shacl-form. For each file the user chooses to keep the local version, take the remote version, or skip the file for this push.
