docs.title: VirtualFilesystem
docs.text:
File: modules/filesystem-manager/virtual-filesystem/index.js

A sub-module of adwlm-filesystem-manager. Provides a Git-backed virtual filesystem that persists in the browser's Origin Private File System (opfs-directory-filesystem.js) or in a local folder (fsa-directory-filesystem.js). Network operations use the GitHub/GitLab API provider (api-provider.js).

docs.title: Key Methods
docs.text: Method Description add_repository(metadata) Loads a remote repository via the API ({ folder, url, username, token, branch, use_lazy_loading }): with lazy loading only the file tree is fetched (.remote-tree.json), otherwise all files are downloaded. Then runs git init, adds the remote and stores credentials add_local_repository(...) Registers a local folder (File System Access API) as repository remove_repository(path) Recursively deletes all files from the virtual FS (for local folders: forgets the folder handle) list_repository_names() Lists the repositories in the virtual FS root plus the registered local folders list_branches(metadata) Fetches the remote's branch list via the API list_entries_from_workdir(repo, folder) Lists files and subdirectories for a given folder (working directory merged with the lazy-loading manifest) read_file(repo, path) Reads a file as a string (downloads it first if lazy loading is used) read_directory_files(repo, folder) Reads all files of a folder (used to append indexes/*.ttl to the shapes) save_and_stage_file(repo, contents, path) Writes a file, stages it and tracks it in .dirty.json / .snapshot.json list_staged_files(repo) Reads .dirty.json; deleted files get a -deleted suffix commit_and_push_file(repo, staged, selected, message) Pushes the selected files as one commit via the API (pushViaApi) pull(repo) Downloads changed files via the API; returns { changedPaths, deletedPaths } for incremental index updates checkPushConflicts(...) Compares the files to be pushed with their current remote versions resolveConflictWithRemote(...) Replaces a local file with its remote version unstageFile(repo, path) Restores the last synchronised version from .snapshot.json, or deletes a new, never-pushed file get_credentials(...) / update_credentials(...) Reads / changes username and token has_remote(repo) / has_token(repo) Checks whether sharing / synchronising is possible generate_indexes_for_saved_file(repo, path, isDeleted) Updates indexes/<folder>.ttl for one file generate_indexes_for_all_files(repo, folderNames) Rebuilds the index files for all files of the given folders

docs.title: Entity Editor
docs.text:
adwlm-entity-editor

File: modules/entity-editor/index.js

The main editing area. Wraps the shacl-form component and manages the lifecycle of the currently open entity.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Render the shacl-form for the currently selected entity
  • Load the correct SHACL shape for the entity type and append the content of all indexes/*.ttl files of the repository to it, so linked entity dropdowns are populated
  • Track unsaved changes and guard against accidental navigation
  • Dispatch save requests; block saving if the form is invalid
  • Handle "quick add" — creating a new linked entity from within an open form
  • Show linked entities in a draggable, resizable floating side panel (read-only preview)
  • Automatically link new works and manifestations to the default data collections
  • Reload the indexes (Reload indexes button), copy the entity IRI, delete the entity

docs.title: Key Properties
docs.text: Property Type Description entity_to_edit Object Currently open entity: { contents, path, entity_iri, entity_type, shapesUrl } entity_type_definitions Array Entity type definitions loaded from editor-default.ttl ui_language String Current UI language _hasUnsavedChanges Boolean Set to true on any change event from shacl-form _selected_repository_path String Kept in sync with the filesystem manager via events _cachedConfig Object Cached result of configuration/config.json — cleared on repository change

docs.title: Events Dispatched
docs.text: Event When Payload adwlm-entity-editor:entity-to-save Save button clicked { entity_iri, rdf_contents, json_ld_contents, path, shapesUrl } adwlm-entity-editor:unsaved-changes Unsaved-changes state changes { hasUnsavedChanges: Boolean } adwlm-entity-editor:entity-to-delete Delete button clicked — adwlm-entity-editor:cached-config Repository config.json read { datasetBaseUrl, projectDomain } adwlm-quick-add:entity-to-save Quick-add form saved same payload as entity-to-save plus isQuickAdd: true adwlm-entity-search:reload-indexes Reload indexes button clicked — entity-selected "Edit" in the side panel { filename }

docs.title: Events Consumed
docs.text: Event Source Effect adwlm-filesystem-manager:clear-entity-editor Filesystem manager Clears the current form adwlm-filesystem-manager:repository-selected Filesystem manager Updates repository path; clears config cache adwlm-filesystem-manager:item-selected Filesystem manager Updates repository path; clears config cache adwlm-filesystem-manager:quick-add-indexed Filesystem manager Appends the new index entry to the form and selects the new entity adwlm-filesystem-manager:file-changed-remotely Filesystem manager Reloads the open entity adwlm-entity-types-dialog:entity-to-add Entity types dialog Creates a new empty entity of the selected type adwlm-graph-view:preview-entity Graph view Opens the side panel for the entity shacl-form:quick-add shacl-form (shadow DOM) Opens the quick-add dialog for a linked entity field

docs.title: Entity ID Generation
docs.text:
New entity IRIs are generated at creation time using the Web Crypto API:

_generate_entity_id() {
    let array = new Uint32Array(1);
    self.crypto.getRandomValues(array);
    return array[0]; // random 32-bit unsigned integer
}

The IRI is built as <projectDomain><folder>/<IDprefix><id> (projectDomain defaults to urn:uuid:, IDprefix per folder is optional, both from config.json). This produces paths like persons/2847362910.ttl and IRIs like <urn:uuid:persons/2847362910>.

docs.title: Quick Add
docs.text: When shacl-form dispatches shacl-form:quick-add, the editor resolves the entity type from the classIri (removing a trailing Entity, e.g. melod:PlaceEntity → melod:Place) and opens an sl-dialog with its own shacl-form. Its Save button is enabled once the form is valid. After saving, the filesystem manager updates the index and dispatches quick-add-indexed; the editor then appends the new index entry to the originating form and selects the new entity in the dropdown.

docs.title: Side Panel (Linked Entity Preview)
docs.text: When a user clicks a link inside a shacl-form field (links are rendered as <a class="uuid">), the editor intercepts the click using composedPath() to pierce the shadow DOM, reads the linked .ttl file from the virtual filesystem, and renders it in a floating, draggable and resizable panel using a second shacl-form instance in read-only data-view mode. The panel can also be opened from the graph view.

docs.title: Repository Configuration Cache
docs.text: On first load of a repository, the editor reads configuration/config.json. The result is cached in _cachedConfig and cleared when a different repository is selected. This avoids repeated filesystem reads for every entity opened in the same session.

docs.title: Entity Search
docs.text:
adwlm-entity-search

File: modules/entity-search/index.js

The search panel. Provides full-text search across all entity labels, alternative labels and classifications in the active repository.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Loads the index files of the repository (one .ttl per entity type, listed in INDEXES in modules/services/index-store-service.js) into the shared Oxigraph store of the index store service
  • Runs multiple SPARQL queries to extract entity metadata: types, labels, composers, classifications, and alternative labels
  • Filters results by label text (including alternative labels and classifications) and/or entity type
  • On selection, calls selectEntityInTree() of the filesystem manager (fallback: dispatches entity-selected) to open the matching file

docs.title: Events Dispatched
docs.text: Event When Payload entity-selected Search result clicked { path: String } — navigates the tree

docs.title: Events Consumed
docs.text: Event Source Effect adwlm-filesystem-manager:repository-selected Filesystem manager Updates the repository path adwlm-entity-editor:cached-config Entity editor Sets the config and loads indexes adwlm-entity-search:reload-indexes Filesystem manager, entity editor Clears the Oxigraph store and reloads all index files adwlm-entity-search:clear-indexes Filesystem manager Clears the search adwlm-index-store:loaded Index store service Rebuilds the result entries

docs.title: How Indexes Work
docs.text:
The search component reads the index files from the indexes/ folder of the local copy of the repository. These files are generated by the CI/CD pipeline of the data repository after each push, and the editor keeps them up to date itself whenever an entity is saved, deleted, unstaged or pulled (see Datasets Generation).

Implication: the search index reflects the locally saved state, including changes that have not been pushed yet. After each of these operations, adwlm-entity-search:reload-indexes triggers a fresh reload of all indexes in search and graph view.

docs.title: SPARQL Queries
docs.text: The search component executes four separate SPARQL queries against the Oxigraph store and combines the results:

docs.title: Query 1: Subjects and Types
docs.text:
SELECT DISTINCT ?subject ?type WHERE {
  ?subject a ?type .
}
ORDER BY ?subject

docs.title: Query 2: Labels (Label, Composer)
docs.text:
SELECT ?subject ?label ?type ?composer WHERE {
  ?subject <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#prefLabel> ?title .
  OPTIONAL {
    ?subject <https://schema.org/composer> ?composer .
  }
  bind(coalesce(concat(?composer, ": ", ?title), ?title) AS ?label) .
}

This query extracts the primary label for each entity. If a composer is present in the index, the label is formatted as "composer: title". Otherwise, only the title is used.

docs.title: Query 3: Classifications
docs.text:
SELECT ?subject ?classification WHERE {
  ?subject <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#broader> ?classification .
}

Retrieves the broader (parent) classifications for each entity. These are stored in a classificationsMap indexed by subject.

docs.title: Query 4: Alternative Labels
docs.text:
SELECT ?subject ?altlabel WHERE {
  ?subject <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#altLabel> ?altlabel .
}

Retrieves alternative labels for each entity. These are stored in an altLabelsMap indexed by subject.

docs.title: How Results are Combined
docs.text:
After executing all four queries, the results are merged into a single array of entry objects:

{
  subject: "urn:uuid:works/1031334055",
  label: ["Suite in G Major"],
  type: "https://lod.academy/melod/vocab/ontology#WorkEntity",
  classifications: ["concert", "..."],
  altlabels: ["Alternative Name", "Alternate Title"],
  composer: ["Suite in G Major"]  // filled with the same values as label if no composer is part of the index
}

docs.title: Graph View
docs.text:
adwlm-graph-view

File: modules/graph-view/index.js

The Graph tab of the output panel. Shows the entities related to the currently open entity.

  • Properties: entity_to_edit, entity_type_definitions, ui_language
  • Data: reads skos:related and skos:prefLabel from the shared index store (incoming and outgoing relations)
  • Views: SVG graph (pan/zoom, expand a node, at most 8 children before a "+N more" node) or list view, with a type filter and legend; colours per type are defined in TYPE_COLORS
  • Events: listens to adwlm-index-store:loaded; the eye icon on a node dispatches adwlm-graph-view:preview-entity ({ relativePath }) to open the side panel of the entity editor

docs.title: RDF-XML Converter
docs.text:
Directory: modules/rdf-xml-converter/

Converts entity data from JSON-LD (produced by shacl-form.serialize("application/ld+json")) to MEI/XML or TEI/XML for the XML output tab.

Structure:

  • converters/ — one JavaScript module per entity type (e.g. person.js, performance-event.js). Each exports a class (e.g. PersonConverter) with a static toXML(jsonLd) method that collects the values from the flat JSON-LD array into a data object.
  • templates/ — one module per entity type (e.g. person.js) exporting a function generate<Type>XML(data) that returns the formatted MEI/XML or TEI/XML string.
  • types/index.js — JSDoc @typedef definitions of the data objects (e.g. PersonData, WorkData).

How it works:

  1. The form content changes → adwlm-entity-editor calls shacl-form.serialize("application/ld+json")
  2. js/index.js receives the JSON-LD and looks up the correct converter by entity type IRI
  3. The converter fills in the MEI/XML template and returns the result
  4. The XML tab displays the result

Each converter is independent. Adding a new entity type requires only a new converter and template — no changes to shared orchestration code.

docs.title: Datasets Generation
docs.text: This document explains how MerMEId MeLODy generates and uses datasets for search indexes, dropdown menus and the graph view. Understanding this process is essential for setting up a data repository, customizing search behavior, and extending the system with new entity types.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Datasets are aggregated RDF/Turtle files generated from your repository's data. They serve three functions in the editor:

  1. Search indexes — power the entity search functionality that loads in the editor
  2. Cross-reference dropdowns — supply the linked entity fields (e.g., "Birth Place", "Contributor") in the editor forms
  3. Graph view — provide the relations between entities

The index files are kept up to date in two ways:

  • In the editor — whenever you save, delete, unstage or synchronise an entity, the editor updates the corresponding index file directly in the browser. The updated index file is staged and shared together with your data.
  • In the CI/CD pipeline — after every push to main, a pipeline in the data repository regenerates all index files and commits them back to the repository.

Without index files, the editor can read and edit entities, but the search, the graph view and the cross-reference dropdowns are empty.

docs.title: In the Editor
docs.text:
When an entity is saved, deleted or changed by a synchronisation, VirtualFilesystem.generate_indexes_for_saved_file():

  1. Determines the entity folder from the file path (e.g. persons)
  2. Fetches the SPARQL query modules/datasets-generator/<folder>.sparql from the editor
  3. Runs the CONSTRUCT query on the saved file with Oxigraph in the browser
  4. Replaces the triples of this entity in indexes/<folder>.ttl (or removes them for a deleted file); the index file is created if it does not exist
  5. Stages the index file and reloads the search

Because only the changed file is processed, context that a query takes from other folders (e.g. the place name of a venue or institution) may be missing until the CI/CD pipeline regenerates the index.

docs.title: The Pipeline
docs.text:
The template repository includes a GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/pages.yml, "Build and Push Indexes") or a GitLab CI pipeline (.gitlab-ci.yml) that regenerates all datasets after every push to main:

Push to main
    ↓
Job fetch_sparql_queries
  - Download the current SPARQL queries from the editor repository
    ↓
Job generate_datasets
  - Run datasets-generator.sh
  - For each dataset:
      - Collect all RDF files from their source directory
      - Execute a SPARQL CONSTRUCT query
      - Output aggregated .ttl file to indexes/
    ↓
Job push-indexes (GitLab: push_indexes)
  - Commit the indexes/ folder with "Updated indexes [skip ci]"
  - Push to main
    ↓
Synchronise in the editor to receive the updated indexes

The [skip ci] tag in the commit message prevents the pipeline from running again for its own commit.

docs.title: Tools Used
docs.text:
The generation process requires:

  • static-publishing-backend Docker container — provides the RDF aggregator and SPARQL engine
  • SPARQL CONSTRUCT queries — transform entity data into searchable datasets. The queries are maintained in the editor repository (MerMEId-MeLODy/modules/datasets-generator/) and are downloaded at build time by fetch-sparql-queries.sh. Set the variable EDITOR_REPO_REF to use another branch or tag of the editor (default: main). Copies of the queries in the data repository are not used.
  • GitHub Actions / GitLab CI — orchestrates the workflow on every push

All of these are configured in the template; you do not need to set anything up manually. The pipeline only needs permission to push to main (see Getting Started).

docs.title: Dataset Files
docs.text:
When the pipeline runs, it generates Turtle (.ttl) files in the indexes/ directory. Each dataset corresponds to an entity type. All entries are typed with an index class melod:<Type>Entity (e.g. melod:PersonEntity), which the SHACL shapes use for linked entity fields.

Dataset File Source Directory Entity Type Used For persons.ttl persons/ Person Search, cross-references (e.g., contributors, publishers) works.ttl works/ Work Search, cross-references (e.g., related works) expressions.ttl expressions/ Expression Search, cross-references (related expressions, works and manifestations) manifestations.ttl manifestations/ Manifestation Search, cross-references (related manifestations) items.ttl items/ Item Search, cross-references (related manifestations and items) institutions.ttl institutions/ Institution Search, cross-references (e.g., holding institutions/repositories) places.ttl places/ Place Search, cross-references (e.g., birth place) venues.ttl venues/ Venue Search, cross-references (e.g. performance venue) events.ttl events/ Event Search, cross-references (e.g. historic events of a items creation) performanceEvents.ttl performanceEvents/ Performance Event Search, cross-references (e.g. first performance of an expression) instrumentations.ttl instrumentations/ Instrumentation Search, cross-references (e.g. instrumentation of an expression) bibliography.ttl bibliography/ Bibliography Search, cross-references (e.g. evidences of a performance or work) letters.ttl letters/ Letter Search, cross-references dataCollections.ttl dataCollections/ Data Collection Search, cross-references (data collections of works and manifestations) dataCatalogs.ttl dataCatalogs/ Data Catalog Cross-references (data catalog of a data collection)

The search and the graph view load the index files listed in INDEXES in modules/services/index-store-service.js (all of the above except dataCatalogs.ttl). For the form dropdowns, all files in indexes/ are used.

docs.title: SPARQL Query Reference
docs.text:
Each dataset is built using a SPARQL CONSTRUCT query that transforms entity data into a simplified searchable form. These queries are located in the editor repository in modules/datasets-generator/.

All queries output the index class (a melod:<Type>Entity) and skos:prefLabel; most of them also output skos:related links to connected entities, which are used by the graph view.

docs.title: Persons Dataset
docs.text:
File: persons.sparql

Purpose: Index all persons with their full names.

Output properties:

  • skos:prefLabel — formatted name (e.g., "Bach, Johann Sebastian")

Query logic:

  • Combines schema:familyName and schema:givenName into a displayable label
  • Falls back to family name only if given name is missing
  • Sorted alphabetically by full name

docs.title: Works Dataset
docs.text:
File: works.sparql

Purpose: Index all works with titles, alternative titles and classifications.

Output properties:

  • skos:prefLabel — main title
  • skos:altLabel — uniform title, alternative titles and other titles (if present)
  • skos:broader — work classification (if present)
  • skos:related — expressions, contributors, work parts, bibliography and data collections

Query logic:

  • Extracts the main title (type: MainTitle)
  • Optionally includes uniform, alternative and other titles as searchable variants
  • Sorted by main title

docs.title: Expressions Dataset
docs.text:
File: expressions.sparql

Purpose: Index all expressions with labels including position and incipit text for identification.

Output properties:

  • skos:prefLabel — expression label with optional position and incipit text
  • skos:broader — classification (if present)
  • skos:related — performances, first performance, place of creation, contributors, parts, components, historic events, instrumentation, bibliography, MEI incipit

Query logic:

  • Uses rdfs:label as base label (falls back to the IRI)
  • Optionally prepends the position and appends the incipit text in parentheses for disambiguation
  • Sorted by label

docs.title: Manifestations Dataset
docs.text:
File: manifestations.sparql

Purpose: Index all manifestations with their titles and classifications.

Output properties:

  • skos:prefLabel — manifestation title (with title type)
  • skos:broader — classification (if present)
  • skos:related — embodied expressions, parts, data collections, contributors, publisher, place of publication

Query logic:

  • Extracts title from title subject (falls back to the IRI)
  • Optionally includes classification for broader search
  • Sorted by title

docs.title: Items Dataset
docs.text:
File: items.sparql

Purpose: Index all items with titles and classifications.

Output properties:

  • skos:prefLabel — item label
  • skos:broader — classification
  • skos:related — manifestation, current keeper, parts, hands, provenance agents

Query logic:

  • Uses item label from rdfs:label (falls back to the IRI)
  • Includes classification
  • Sorted by label

docs.title: Institutions Dataset
docs.text:
File: institutions.sparql

Purpose: Index all institutions with abbreviations or RISM sigla.

Output properties:

  • skos:prefLabel — label with optional abbreviation or RISM siglum
  • skos:broader — ("Organization" or "RISM") and place name, if present
  • skos:related — place

Query logic:

  • Uses institution name as base
  • Prepends abbreviation or RISM siglum if available: "DB (Name)"
  • Falls back to name only if no abbreviation or rism siglum
  • Sorted by label

docs.title: Places Dataset
docs.text:
File: places.sparql

Purpose: Index all places with their names.

Output properties:

  • skos:prefLabel — place name

Query logic:

  • Extracts place name from schema:name
  • Sorted alphabetically

docs.title: Venues Dataset
docs.text:
File: venues.sparql

Purpose: Index all venues with their names and locations.

Output properties:

  • skos:prefLabel — venue name
  • skos:broader — place name (if venue is located in a place)
  • skos:related — place

Query logic:

  • Extracts venue name from schema:name
  • Optionally includes containing place via schema:containedInPlace
  • Sorted by venue name

docs.title: Events Dataset
docs.text:
File: events.sparql

Purpose: Index all events with their names.

Output properties:

  • skos:prefLabel — event name
  • skos:related — place, contributors, bibliography

Query logic:

  • Extracts event name from rdfs:label
  • Sorted by name

docs.title: Performance Events Dataset
docs.text:
File: performanceEvents.sparql

Purpose: Index all performance events with dates and venues.

Output properties:

  • skos:prefLabel — performance label with optional date and venue
  • skos:related — contributors, venue, bibliography

Query logic:

  • Uses performance event name as base
  • Optionally appends date and venue information for context
  • Combined label format: "Name: Date Place"
  • Sorted by label

docs.title: Instrumentations Dataset
docs.text:
File: instrumentations.sparql

Purpose: Index all instrumentations.

Output properties:

  • skos:prefLabel — instrumentation name
  • skos:related — instrumentation groups

Query logic:

  • Extracts name from rdfs:label (falls back to the IRI)
  • Sorted alphabetically

docs.title: Bibliography Dataset
docs.text:
File: bibliography.sparql

Purpose: Index all bibliography entries with abbreviations or titles.

Output properties:

  • skos:prefLabel — bibliography label with abbreviation or title
  • skos:related — authors, editors, publisher, place, keeper

Query logic:

  • Prefers melod:hasAbbreviation if present
  • Falls back to title if no abbreviation exists
  • Sorted by label

docs.title: Letters Dataset
docs.text:
File: letters.sparql

Purpose: Index all letters.

Output properties:

  • skos:prefLabel — title of the letter
  • skos:related — participants, places, holding institution

Query logic:

  • Extracts the title from rdfs:label
  • Sorted by label

docs.title: Data Collections Dataset
docs.text:
File: dataCollections.sparql

Purpose: Index all data collections.

Output properties:

  • skos:prefLabel — name of the data collection (class melod:DataCollectionEntity)

docs.title: Data Catalogs Dataset
docs.text:
File: dataCatalogs.sparql

Purpose: Index the data catalog of the repository.

Output properties:

  • skos:prefLabel — name of the data catalog (class melod:DataCatalog)

docs.title: The Generation Script
docs.text:
The file modules/datasets-generator/datasets-generator.sh in the data repository (see the GitHub template) orchestrates the entire process. It:

  1. Sets up directory paths for all entity types

  2. For each dataset, calls the rdf-data-aggregator tool with:

    • Source directory: where entity files are located (e.g., persons/)
    • File pattern: which files to include (e.g., *.ttl)
    • SPARQL query: the transformation logic, downloaded before by fetch-sparql-queries.sh (e.g., sparql-queries/persons.sparql)
    • Output path: where to write the result (e.g., indexes/persons.ttl)

  3. Times each operation for performance monitoring

Example invocation: 

/static-publishing-backend rdf-data-aggregator \
  $persons_dir_path/ \
  "*.ttl" \
  $datasets_generator_dir_path/persons.sparql \
  $indexes_dir_path/persons.ttl

The script modules/datasets-generator/fetch-sparql-queries.sh downloads all queries listed in its loop from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/music-metadata-tools/MerMEId-MeLODy/$EDITOR_REPO_REF/modules/datasets-generator/.

docs.title: Committing the Indexes
docs.text:
After datasets are generated, the pipeline commits them to the repository:

  1. Datasets are created in the indexes/ directory
  2. The job push-indexes (GitLab: push_indexes) commits the folder with the message Updated indexes [skip ci] — only for the main branch and only if something has changed
  3. The commit is pushed to main; the editor receives the new indexes when you synchronise

Required configuration:

  • GitHub: the workflow requests contents: write itself. If your organisation restricts workflow permissions or main is protected, allow GitHub Actions to push to main.
  • GitLab: the job pushes with the CI/CD job token. Allow Git push requests with the job token in Settings → CI/CD → Job token permissions, or adapt the job to use a project access token.

docs.title: Data Validation
docs.text:
The GitHub template additionally includes a Data Validation workflow (.github/workflows/validate.yml). It is started manually (Actions → Data Validation → Run workflow) and validates the .ttl files of the data folders against the SHACL shapes of the editor (fetched from the main branch of the editor repository).

It can also be run locally with Node.js:

npm install
npm test

docs.title: Datasets Are Not Generated or Not Up to Date
docs.text:
Problem: Dropdowns are empty or search doesn't work.

Solutions:

  1. Check that the indexes/ folder exists in your repository and contains files
  2. Click Reload indexes in the editor toolbar
  3. Synchronise the repository to receive indexes committed by the pipeline
  4. Check that the latest pipeline run ("Build and Push Indexes") succeeded (Actions tab in GitHub, Build → Pipelines in GitLab) and that it was allowed to push to main
  5. Verify that datasetBaseUrl in config.json is set (any non-empty value)

docs.title: SPARQL Query Errors
docs.text:
Problem: Pipeline fails with a SPARQL error.

Solutions:

  1. Check the Actions logs for the specific error
  2. Verify namespace prefixes are defined (prefix melod:, prefix skos:, etc.)
  3. Ensure the entity type in the query matches your actual entity classes
  4. Test the query locally in an RDF editor or SPARQL IDE

docs.title: Dataset File Not Generated
docs.text:
Problem: A specific dataset file is missing.

Solutions:

  1. Check the source directory exists and contains .ttl files
  2. Verify the SPARQL query file exists in modules/datasets-generator/ of the editor repository — the editor finds a query by the folder name (<folder>.sparql)
  3. Ensure the query is listed in fetch-sparql-queries.sh and an entry is added to datasets-generator.sh of the data repository
  4. Check that no syntax errors exists in the SPARQL query

docs.title: Related Topics
docs.text:
• Repository Configuration — datasetBaseUrl and projectDomain settings
  • SHACL Shapes — how form fields reference datasets
  • Entity Types — data model and entity classes
  • Data Model Ontologies — vocabularies used in datasets

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: MerMEId MeLODy is configured at two distinct levels: the editor itself (which entity types are available and how their forms look) and the data repository (IRI scheme and ID prefixes). SHACL shape files provide a third layer of configuration, driving the form fields for each entity type.

docs.title: At a Glance
docs.text:
Editor repository
├── configuration/
│   ├── editor-default.ttl    ← which entity types exist and which SHACL shape each uses
│   └── *.shacl               ← one shape file per entity type, defines form fields
└── modules/datasets-generator/
    └── <folder>.sparql       ← one SPARQL query per entity folder, builds the index files

Data repository
├── configuration/
│   └── config.json           ← datasetBaseUrl, projectDomain and optional IDprefix
└── indexes/
    └── <folder>.ttl          ← generated index files (search and dropdowns)

No build step is required for most configuration changes. Editing a SHACL shape or editor-default.ttl takes effect immediately on the next page load.

docs.title: Editor Configuration
docs.text: The editor configuration file configuration/editor-default.ttl is a Turtle file loaded at startup. It tells the editor which entity types are available, what their display names are in each UI language, where their files are stored, and which SHACL shape file defines their form.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
When the editor starts, js/index.js fetches editor-default.ttl and loads its content into an in-browser Oxigraph triple store. A SPARQL SELECT query then extracts all entity type definitions for the current UI language:

SELECT ?type ?label ?folder ?shacl WHERE {
  ?type a melod:EntityType ;
        rdfs:label ?label ;
        melod:entity_folder_name ?folder ;
        melod:shacl_file_location ?shacl .
}

The results are passed to the adwlm-entity-editor, adwlm-filesystem-manager and adwlm-graph-view components as entity_type_definitions. This drives the "New entity" dialog, tells the editor which SHACL shape to load when a file of that type is opened, and determines which folders are shown in the repository tree. The query is run again whenever the UI language is changed.

docs.title: Registration Format
docs.text:
Each entity type is an RDF subject with four required properties:

@prefix melod: <https://lod.academy/melod/vocab/ontology#> .
@prefix rdfs:  <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .

melod:Person a melod:Entity ;
    rdfs:label "Person"@en , "Person"@de ;
    melod:entity_folder_name "persons" ;
    melod:shacl_file_location "configuration/person.shacl" .

docs.title: The Four Properties
docs.text:
Property Description a melod:Entity Required type declaration — the SPARQL query matches on this rdfs:label Human-readable display name shown in the "New entity" dialog (e.g. "Person"@en). One label per UI language (@en, @de) is required — a type without a label in the current language does not appear in the editor melod:entity_folder_name Name of the folder in the data repository where files of this type are stored (e.g. "persons") — must match the actual folder name exactly melod:shacl_file_location Path or URL of the SHACL shape file for this entity type

The data catalog (melod:DataCatalog, dataCatalogs/catalog.ttl) is not registered in editor-default.ttl; it is edited via the catalog metadata dialog with configuration/dataCatalog.shacl.

docs.title: SHACL File Locations
docs.text:
The melod:shacl_file_location value can be either:

  • A relative path within the editor repository: e.g. "configuration/person.shacl" — resolved against the editor's base URL at runtime
  • An absolute HTTPS URL: e.g. "https://example.org/shapes/person.shacl" — fetched directly

Using an absolute URL allows you to host SHACL shapes on an external server or in the data repository and reference them without modifying the editor files. This is useful when managing multiple data repositories that share the same entity type definitions but may have different field configurations.

docs.title: Adding a New Entity Type
docs.text: To add a custom entity type to the editor:

docs.title: Step 1 — Create a SHACL shape
docs.text: Create a .shacl file (which is a valid Turtle file) in the configuration/ folder. Define the node shape for your entity type. See SHACL Shapes for the properties to use.

docs.title: Step 2 — Register the entity type
docs.text:
Add a new block to configuration/editor-default.ttl:

melod:MyNewType a melod:Entity ;
    rdfs:label "My New Type"@en , "Mein neuer Typ"@de ;
    melod:entity_folder_name "mynewtype" ;
    melod:shacl_file_location "configuration/mynewtype.shacl" .

Replace melod:MyNewType with the full class IRI from your ontology. Update the labels, folder name, and shape file path accordingly.

docs.title: Step 3 — Create the data folder
docs.text: Create the folder (e.g. mynewtype/) in the data repository. If it does not exist, it is created when the first entity of this type is saved.

docs.title: Step 4 — Add a search index entry (optional)
docs.text:
If you want the new entity type to be searchable, add a SPARQL query modules/datasets-generator/mynewtype.sparql to the editor and an entry for its index file to INDEXES in modules/services/index-store-service.js. See Extending the Editor for details.

No changes to the core editor components are needed for the form — it is generated automatically from the SHACL shape.

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• The entity_folder_name must exactly match the folder name in the data repository. A mismatch means the editor cannot find existing files of that type in the tree and will write new files to the wrong path.
  • The SHACL shape is not cached between sessions — it is fetched fresh each time a file of that type is opened.
  • Entity type definitions from editor-default.ttl are loaded once at startup. After editing this file, reload the page.

docs.title: Extending the Editor
docs.text: MerMEId MeLODy is designed to be extended with little changes to the core components. Adding a new entity type requires a SHACL shape, an entry in editor-default.ttl, and — to make it searchable and linkable — a SPARQL index query and an INDEXES entry. Optionally you can add a colour for the graph view and an MEI/XML converter.

docs.title: At a Glance
docs.text:
Editor repository
├── configuration/
│   ├── editor-default.ttl            ← which entity types exist and which SHACL shape each uses
│   └── *.shacl                       ← one shape file per entity type, defines form fields
├── modules/datasets-generator/
│   └── <folder>.sparql               ← index query per entity folder
├── modules/services/index-store-service.js  ← INDEXES: index files loaded for search and graph
└── modules/rdf-xml-converter/        ← optional MEI/XML converters

Data repository
├── configuration/
│   └── config.json                   ← datasetBaseUrl, projectDomain, IDprefix
└── indexes/                          ← generated index files

No build step is required for most configuration changes. Editing a SHACL shape or editor-default.ttl takes effect immediately on the next page load.

docs.title: Editor Configuration
docs.text: The editor configuration file configuration/editor-default.ttl is a Turtle file loaded at startup. It tells the editor which entity types are available, what their display names are, where their files are stored, and which SHACL shape file defines their form.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
When the editor starts, js/index.js fetches editor-default.ttl and loads its content into an in-browser Oxigraph triple store. A SPARQL SELECT query then extracts all entity type definitions with the label in the current UI language:

SELECT ?entity_type ?entity_name ?entity_folder_name ?shacl_file_location WHERE {
  ?entity_type a melod:Entity ;
        rdfs:label ?entity_name ;
        melod_ui:entity_folder_name ?entity_folder_name ;
        melod_ui:shacl_file_location ?shacl_file_location .
  FILTER (lang(?entity_name) = '<current UI language>')
}

The results are passed to the adwlm-entity-editor, adwlm-filesystem-manager and adwlm-graph-view components as entity_type_definitions. This drives the "New entity" dialog and tells the editor which SHACL shape to load when a file of that type is opened.

docs.title: Registration Format
docs.text:
Each entity type is an RDF subject with four required properties:

@prefix melod: <https://lod.academy/melod/vocab/ontology#> .
@prefix rdfs:  <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .
@prefix melod_ui: <https://lod.academy/melod/vocab/ui/> .

melod:Person a melod:Entity ;
    rdfs:label "Person"@en , "Person"@de ;
    melod_ui:entity_folder_name "persons" ;
    melod_ui:shacl_file_location "configuration/person.shacl" .

docs.title: The Four Properties
docs.text: Property Description a melod:Entity Required type declaration — the SPARQL query matches on this rdfs:label Human-readable display name shown in the "New entity" dialog — one label per UI language (@en, @de) melod_ui:entity_folder_name Name of the folder in the data repository where files of this type are stored (e.g. "persons") — must match the actual folder name exactly melod_ui:shacl_file_location Path or URL of the SHACL shape file for this entity type

docs.title: SHACL File Locations
docs.text:
The melod_ui:shacl_file_location value can be either:

  • A relative path within the editor repository: e.g. "configuration/person.shacl" — resolved against the editor's base URL at runtime
  • An absolute HTTPS URL: e.g. "https://example.org/shapes/person.shacl" — fetched directly

Using an absolute URL allows you to host SHACL shapes on an external server or in the data repository and reference them without modifying the editor files. This is useful when managing multiple data repositories that share the same entity type definitions but may have different field configurations.

docs.title: Step 1 — Create a SHACL shape
docs.text:
Create a new .shacl file in configuration/. This is a Turtle file that defines the form fields for your entity type. Give labels and descriptions in every UI language.

@prefix sh:     <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#> .
@prefix melod:  <https://lod.academy/melod/vocab/ontology#> .
@prefix rdfs:   <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .
@prefix xsd:    <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> .
@prefix schema: <https://schema.org/> .

melod:MyNewType
    a sh:NodeShape, rdfs:Class ;
    sh:property [
        sh:path schema:name ;
        sh:name "Name"@en, "Name"@de ;
        sh:minCount 1 ;
        sh:maxCount 1 ;
        sh:datatype xsd:string ;
    ] ;
    sh:property [
        sh:path schema:description ;
        sh:name "Description"@en, "Beschreibung"@de ;
        sh:datatype xsd:string ;
    ] ;
    sh:targetClass melod:MyNewType .

Save the file as configuration/mynewtype.shacl.

See SHACL Shapes for the full property reference.

docs.title: Step 2 — Register the entity type
docs.text:
Open configuration/editor-default.ttl and add a new block:

melod:MyNewType a melod:Entity ;
    rdfs:label "My New Type"@en , "Mein neuer Typ"@de ;
    melod_ui:entity_folder_name "mynewtypes" ;
    melod_ui:shacl_file_location "configuration/mynewtype.shacl" .
  • Replace melod:MyNewType with the full class IRI from your ontology (e.g. melod:MyNewType if the class is defined in the MeLODy ontology, or any other IRI if you're using a different namespace)
  • rdfs:label is the display name shown in the "New entity" dialog; without a label in the current UI language the type is not shown
  • melod_ui:entity_folder_name must exactly match the folder name you will create in Step 3
  • melod_ui:shacl_file_location can be a relative path or an absolute HTTPS URL

docs.title: Step 3 — Add a dataset and search index (optional)
docs.text: If you want your new entity type to appear in the search panel, in the graph view or want to cross reference an entity, you need an index query and an entry in the index list.

docs.title: Create a SPARQL query
docs.text:
Add a new .sparql file in modules/datasets-generator/ of the editor repository. The file name must equal the folder name (mynewtypes.sparql): the editor uses it to update indexes/mynewtypes.ttl in the data repository whenever an entity is saved, and the CI/CD pipeline of the data repository fetches it from the editor repository.

prefix melod: <https://lod.academy/melod/vocab/ontology#>
prefix skos: <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#>
prefix schema: <https://schema.org/>

construct {
  ?iri a melod:MyNewTypeEntity ;
    skos:prefLabel ?label .
} where {
  select ?iri ?label where {
    ?iri a melod:MyNewType .
    ?iri schema:name ?label .
  }
  order by ?label
}

Key requirements: - Use CONSTRUCT (not SELECT) to output RDF - Always include skos:prefLabel — the search component and the dropdowns use this property - Type the index entries as melod:<Type>Entity (e.g. melod:MyNewTypeEntity) — linked entity fields in the SHACL shapes refer to this class - Optionally add skos:altLabel and skos:broader for the search, and skos:related for the graph view - Use OPTIONAL for any properties that may not be present on every entity

docs.title: Register in the editor
docs.text:
Add an entry to INDEXES in modules/services/index-store-service.js:

{ name: "MyNewType", url: "mynewtypes.ttl", labels: { en: "My New Type", de: "Mein neuer Typ" } },

Without this entry, the index is not loaded for the search, the type filter and the graph view. (Linked entity dropdowns work independently, because the editor appends all files from indexes/ to the shapes.)

Optionally add a colour for the new type to TYPE_COLORS in modules/graph-view/index.js.

docs.title: Update the CI/CD pipeline of the data repository
docs.text:
Add the query name to the list in modules/datasets-generator/fetch-sparql-queries.sh and add an entry to modules/datasets-generator/datasets-generator.sh of the data repository:

echo "construct the mynewtypes dataset"
time /static-publishing-backend rdf-data-aggregator \
  $CI_PROJECT_DIR/mynewtypes/ "*.ttl" \
  $datasets_generator_dir_path/mynewtypes.sparql \
  $indexes_dir_path/mynewtypes.ttl

docs.title: Update SHACL configuration
docs.text: If the entity type is used in form dropdowns (i.e. as a linked entity field in another shape), reference the index class in the relevant SHACL shapes: sh:class melod:MyNewTypeEntity.

docs.title: Test locally
docs.text:
Dataset generation can be tested locally without pushing (from the root of the data repository, after fetching the queries into sparql-queries/):

sh modules/datasets-generator/fetch-sparql-queries.sh
docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/repo -e GITHUB_WORKSPACE=/repo \
  registry.gitlab.rlp.net/adwmainz/nfdi4culture/cdmd/static-publishing-backend/static-publishing-backend:latest \
  /repo/modules/datasets-generator/datasets-generator.sh

Generated files will appear in indexes/. See Datasets Generation for background on the pipeline and SPARQL query reference.

docs.title: Step 4 — Add a MEI/XML converter (optional)
docs.text:
If you want MEI/XML output in the XML tab for your new entity type, add:

  1. A converter module at modules/rdf-xml-converter/converters/mynewtype.js
  2. An MEI/XML template string at modules/rdf-xml-converter/templates/mynewtype-template.js
  3. A mapping entry in modules/rdf-xml-converter/types/index.js:
import { myNewTypeConverter } from "./converters/mynewtype.js";

export const converters = {
    // ... existing entries ...
    "https://lod.academy/melod/vocab/ontology#MyNewType": myNewTypeConverter,
};

The converter receives the JSON-LD object from shacl-form.serialize("application/ld+json") and must return a complete MEI/XML string.

docs.title: Modifying an Existing Form
docs.text:
To add, remove, or change fields in an existing entity type, edit the corresponding .shacl file in configuration/. No code changes are needed — the form is regenerated from the shape on the next page load.

Common modifications:

  • Add a field: add a new sh:property block with sh:path, sh:name (one per language, e.g. "Name"@en, "Name"@de), sh:datatype, and sh:order or sh:group
  • Make a field required: set sh:minCount 1
  • Restrict to a single value: set sh:maxCount 1
  • Add a dropdown: set sh:in ( "value1" "value2" "value3" )
  • Add a linked entity field: set sh:class melod:SomeTypeEntity (the class of the index entries) and sh:nodeKind sh:IRI
  • Reorder fields: change the sh:order values

docs.title: Hosting SHACL Shapes Externally
docs.text:
The melod:shacl_file_location value in editor-default.ttl accepts any HTTPS URL. This allows you to host your SHACL shapes in a separate repository, on a CDN, or alongside your data repository, and reference them by URL:

melod:MyNewType
    a melod:Entity ;
    rdfs:label "My New Type" ;
    melod:entity_folder_name "mynewtype" ;
    melod:shacl_file_location "https://yourname.github.io/my-shapes/mynewtype.shacl" .

The editor fetches the shape file at runtime for each entity opened. Make sure the URL returns the correct Content-Type (text/turtle or application/octet-stream) and is accessible without authentication.

docs.title: Local Setup
docs.text:
MerMEId can be used directly through the hosted web application. However, some users may prefer to run all components locally, for example when working in restricted network environments, for long-term preservation purposes, or to avoid dependencies on external services.

This page describes how to:

  • Run the editor locally
  • Use a local version of the form editor

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Depending on the setup you choose, you may need:

Feature Required Software Editor only Git, Python 3 Editor with local form editor Git, Python 3, Node.js Fully offline setup Git, Python 3, Node.js Running the tests Git, Node.js (v22 or later)

You can verify that the required software is installed:

git --version
python3 --version
node --version
npm --version

docs.title: Running the Editor Locally
docs.text: The editor is a static web application and does not require a build step.

docs.title: Option 1: Using Python
docs.text:
Clone the repository and start a local web server:

git clone https://github.com/Music-Metadata-Tools/MerMEId-MeLODy.git
cd MerMEId-MeLODy
python3 -m http.server 8080

Open the editor in your browser:

http://localhost:8080

docs.title: Option 2: Using VS Code Live Server
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository.
  2. Open the project folder in VS Code.
  3. Install the Live Server extension.
  4. Click Go Live in the VS Code status bar.

The editor will open automatically in your browser.

docs.title: Using a Local Version of the Form Editor
docs.text:
By default, MerMEId loads the form editor from the published online version. If you would like to use a local copy instead, both repositories should be placed in the same parent directory.

Example:

projects/
├── MerMEId-MeLODy/
└── mermeid-shacl-form/

docs.title: 1. Clone the Repositories
docs.text:
From the shared parent directory:

git clone https://github.com/Music-Metadata-Tools/MerMEId-MeLODy.git

git clone https://github.com/Music-Metadata-Tools/mermeid-shacl-form.git
cd mermeid-shacl-form
git checkout development
npm install

docs.title: 2. Build the Form Editor
docs.text:
npm run build-mermeid

This creates:

dist/form-mermeid.js

docs.title: 3. Configure MerMEId
docs.text:
Open:

MerMEId-MeLODy/index.html

Replace the published URL:

<script type="module" src="https://music-metadata-tools.github.io/mermeid-shacl-form/dist/form-mermeid.js"></script>

with:

<script type="module" src="/mermeid-shacl-form/dist/form-mermeid.js"></script>

and update any matching import statements accordingly.

docs.title: 4. Start a Local Server
docs.text:
From the shared parent directory:

python3 -m http.server 8080

docs.title: 5. Open the Editor
docs.text:
http://localhost:8080/MerMEId-MeLODy

Whenever you rebuild the form editor with:

npm run build-mermeid

simply reload the browser. No server restart is required.

docs.title: Fully Offline Setup
docs.text:
Earlier versions of MerMEId MeLODy routed all Git operations through the public isomorphic-git CORS proxy (https://cors.isomorphic-git.org). This is no longer necessary. Cloning, pulling, pushing and listing branches now call the GitHub API (api.github.com) or the GitLab API (https://<host>/api/v4 and /api/graphql) directly from the browser. Both APIs allow cross-origin requests, so no proxy service is involved.

This means:

  • When you run the editor and the form editor locally (see above), the only external requests are those to your Git host's API and to the CDNs that serve the libraries (Shoelace, Lit, isomorphic-git, Oxigraph).
  • Self-hosted GitLab instances work as long as their API allows cross-origin requests.
  • If you want to avoid the CDNs as well, download the libraries referenced in the importmap and <script> tags of index.html and point the URLs to your local copies.

The constant CORS_PROXY in modules/filesystem-manager/constants.js still exists, but it is only used by legacy code paths that are no longer called. You do not need to change it.

docs.title: Working on a Local Folder
docs.text: In Chromium-based browsers, the Add repository dialog can open a folder on your disk instead of loading a repository from a URL. The editor then reads and writes the files directly in that folder. If the folder has no .git directory, the editor runs git init. Sharing and synchronising still go through the GitHub/GitLab API, using the remote URL in .git/config (SSH remotes are converted to HTTPS for the API calls). You can also commit and push with your local Git client.

docs.title: Editor Only
docs.text:
Use this setup if you simply want to run MerMEId on your local machine.

Requirements:

  • Git
  • Python 3

docs.title: Editor + Local Form Editor
docs.text:
Use this setup if you want to use a locally hosted version of the form editor instead of the published online version.

Requirements:

  • Git
  • Python 3
  • Node.js

docs.title: Fully Offline Setup
docs.text:
Use this setup if you want all editor components to run locally without depending on external services. Note that sharing and synchronising always require network access to your Git host's API.

Requirements:

  • Git
  • Python 3
  • Node.js

docs.title: Repository Configuration
docs.text: Each data repository contains a configuration file at configuration/config.json. This file should always be present and correctly configured. If it is missing or invalid, the editor shows the warning "Using default configuration" and falls back to default values.

docs.title: Location
docs.text:
my-catalogue/
└── configuration/
    └── config.json   ← this file

The editor reads this path relative to the repository root when a repository is loaded. The path cannot be changed.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "datasetBaseUrl": "https://yourname.github.io/my-catalogue/datasets/",
  "projectDomain": "urn:uuid:"
}

docs.title: datasetBaseUrl
docs.text:
The base URL where published dataset index files were hosted in earlier versions (a GitHub Pages or GitLab Pages URL).

Current behaviour: the value is kept for compatibility. The URL itself is currently not used to fetch anything. Keep the value with the template url.

Example: 

"datasetBaseUrl": "https://yourname.github.io/my-catalogue/datasets/"

docs.title: What Are Datasets?
docs.text:
Datasets (index files) are aggregated RDF/Turtle files built from your repository's data, stored in the indexes/ folder of the repository. They are generated by a CI/CD pipeline after each push to main using SPARQL CONSTRUCT queries, and the editor updates them itself whenever you save, delete or synchronise entities. Each dataset corresponds to an entity type:

  • persons.ttl — all persons (indexed by full name)
  • works.ttl — all works (indexed by title)
  • institutions.ttl — all institutions (indexed by name and abbreviation)
  • places.ttl — all places (indexed by name)
  • venues.ttl — all venues (indexed by name and location)
  • manifestations.ttl, expressions.ttl, items.ttl, bibliography.ttl, letters.ttl, dataCollections.ttl, etc.

For a complete list and how each dataset is built, see Datasets Generation.

docs.title: How Datasets Are Used
docs.text:
The index files are used in three ways:

  1. Entity search — the adwlm-entity-search component loads all index files from indexes/ into its Oxigraph SPARQL store. When you search for "Bach" in the editor, it queries these indexes rather than scanning individual entity files.

  2. Cross-reference dropdowns in forms — linked entity fields (e.g., "Contributor", "Birth Place") list the entities of the index files. When a form is opened, the editor appends all files from indexes/ to the SHACL shape, so shacl-form can offer every entity of the requested class (e.g. melod:PlaceEntity).

  3. Graph view — the relations between entities (skos:related) are read from the index files.

Note

The index files reflect the files in your local copy of the repository. The editor updates them on save, and the CI/CD pipeline rebuilds them after every push to main. Changes of other users become visible after synchronising.

docs.title: projectDomain
docs.text:
The IRI prefix used when generating identifiers for new entities.

Default value: "urn:uuid:" — produces opaque identifiers like urn:uuid:persons/2847362910

Alternative: an HTTPS namespace — produces dereferenceable URIs like https://example.org/persons/2847362910

"projectDomain": "https://example.org/"

The projectDomain is also used for the fixed IRIs of the data catalog and the default data collections (<projectDomain>dataCatalogs/catalog, <projectDomain>dataCollections/works, <projectDomain>dataCollections/manifestations).

See Entity IRIs for full details on IRI generation and the implications of changing this value.

Warning

Changing projectDomain after entities have been created does not retroactively update existing entity IRIs. Existing entities keep their original IRIs. New entities will use the new prefix, resulting in a mixed-prefix dataset. Decide on your IRI scheme before creating any entities.

docs.title: IDprefix
docs.text:
A prefix for chosen entity types, which is inserted in front of the identifier number. This configuration is optional.

Default value: "1477695404" — produces opaque identifiers like urn:uuid:works/1477695404

Alternative: an IRI with a prefix to distinguish entity types with a character — for example w1477695404 for works, full IRI: urn:uuid:works/w1477695404. This is done by adding the folder name with the chosen prefix.

Only the entities of the folders named in the config.json will get a prefix.

"IDprefix": {
    "works": "w",
    "persons": "p"
  }

Warning

Changing IDprefix after entities have been created does not retroactively update existing entity IRIs. Existing entities keep their original IRIs. New entities will use the new prefix, resulting in a mixed-prefix dataset. Decide on your IRI scheme before creating any entities.

docs.title: Typical Setup (GitHub)
docs.text:
If you created your repository from the MerMEId MeLODy Template on GitHub, the typical config.json looks like:

{
  "datasetBaseUrl": "https://music-metadata-tools.github.io/MerMEId-MeLODy-Template/datasets/",
  "projectDomain": "urn:uuid:"
}

Keep the config.json shipped with the template; usually only projectDomain (and optionally IDprefix) needs a decision. No GitHub Pages setup is required. Make sure GitHub Actions may push to main, so the Build and Push Indexes workflow can commit the indexes/ folder.

docs.title: Other Repository Files
docs.text:
Besides config.json, every data repository contains files that are managed by the editor:

  • dataCatalogs/catalog.ttl — the data catalog of the repository (melod:DataCatalog), edited via the Catalog metadata button. Fields: name, contributors with roles (data manager, data contributor, editor, contributor, publisher), application ("MerMEId MeLODy"), description.
  • dataCollections/ — data collections (e.g. a work catalogue or a source catalogue) belonging to the data catalog. Fields: name, data catalog, type ("work catalog" / "source catalog"), restrictions of use, status (draft, candidate, approved, published), responsible. The default collections works.ttl ("All works") and manifestations.ttl ("All manifestations") are created automatically; new works and manifestations are added to them.
  • indexes/ — generated index files, see Datasets Generation. Do not edit them by hand.

The catalog files are created automatically when a repository is selected for the first time, if they are missing.

The username and personal access token are not part of config.json — they are stored per user in the browser and can be changed in the Repository settings dialog.

docs.title: Services
docs.text: The service layer provides shared, singleton access points to the virtual filesystem, all Git operations and the search indexes. Components never instantiate their own filesystem directly — they always go through the service.

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
Username and personal access token are stored in the git config of the repository (user.name and user.pat). For repositories added by URL, this config lives in the browser's Origin Private File System (OPFS). For local folders, it is written into the folder's own .git/config on disk — the token is then stored there in plain text.

The credentials are read back before each push or pull operation and can be changed at any time through the repository settings dialog. The token is only sent to the GitHub or GitLab API (as Authorization: Bearer or PRIVATE-TOKEN header).

The add-repository dialog additionally remembers the last folder name, URL and username — but not the token — in localStorage (key lastGitCredentials, see credentials-helper.js).

docs.title: Git Host API
docs.text:
All network operations go directly to the APIs of the Git host, implemented in modules/filesystem-manager/api-provider.js:

  • parseRepoUrl() normalises HTTPS, SSH and GitLab web URLs. Hosts containing github are treated as GitHub, all other hosts as GitLab (API v4). Other Git hosts are not supported.
  • createProvider() returns a GitHub or GitLab provider for listing branches, fetching the file tree, downloading files and fetching single remote files.
  • pushViaApi() creates one commit with all selected files — via the GraphQL mutation createCommitOnBranch on GitHub or the Commits API (POST /projects/:id/repository/commits) on GitLab.
  • Requests that are rate-limited (HTTP 429) are retried automatically, respecting Retry-After.

The constant CORS_PROXY in modules/filesystem-manager/constants.js is still defined, but only used by legacy code paths that are no longer called.

docs.title: Lazy Loading
docs.text: When a repository is added with lazy loading (default), only the remote file tree is fetched and written to .remote-tree.json. Each file is downloaded the first time it is read. Without lazy loading, all files are downloaded at once. The setting is stored per repository in the git config (lazy.enabled).

docs.title: Local Filesystem Mode
docs.text:
VirtualFilesystem also supports direct access to the local filesystem via the File System Access API. When a directory handle is registered via add_local_repository(), the picked folder is used as a normal Git working directory (fsa-directory-filesystem.js); if it contains no .git, git init is run. The folder handles are kept in IndexedDB (local-repository-store.js); after a browser restart, permission is requested again via ensure_local_repository_access().

Sharing and synchronising work exactly as for repositories added by URL (through the GitHub/GitLab API, using the remote from .git/config). The bookkeeping files .dirty.json and .snapshot.json are kept in OPFS under the repository name.

Use case: local workflows for larger repositories, or when you also want to use your local Git client.

Browser support: best supported in Chromium-based browsers (Chrome, Edge). Firefox and Safari do not support the directory picker of the API.

docs.title: Conflict Detection (checkPushConflicts)
docs.text:
Before sharing, checkPushConflicts() is called with the list of selected files. For each file that has a synchronised baseline in .snapshot.json, it:

  1. Fetches the current version of the file from the remote via the API
  2. Compares it with the baseline from the last synchronisation
  3. Reports the file as a conflict if the remote version has changed or the file has been deleted remotely

Conflicting files are shown in the adwlm-push-conflict-dialog, which renders the local and the remote version side by side with shacl-form. For each file the user chooses to keep the local version, take the remote version (resolveConflictWithRemote()), or skip the file for this push. New files that do not exist remotely never cause a conflict.

docs.title: SHACL Shapes
docs.text: Forms in MerMEId MeLODy are generated automatically from SHACL shapes by the shacl-form web component developed by ULB Darmstadt (in the MerMEId fork mermeid-shacl-form). You do not write HTML or JavaScript to add or modify fields — defining them in the SHACL shape file is sufficient.

docs.title: What is a SHACL Shape?
docs.text:
SHACL (Shapes Constraint Language) is a W3C standard for describing and validating RDF data. A "node shape" describes the expected structure of an RDF resource of a given type — its properties, their datatypes, cardinality, and allowed values.

In MerMEId MeLODy, SHACL shapes serve a dual purpose:

  1. Form generation — shacl-form reads the shape and renders an interactive HTML form with the appropriate input widgets
  2. Data validation — the shape constraints (required fields, allowed values, pattern matching) are checked when data is serialised

Each entity type has its own .shacl file, located in configuration/ (in the editor repository or the data repository, depending on how melod:shacl_file_location is configured).

docs.title: Key SHACL Properties for Form Generation
docs.text:
The following properties control how fields appear and behave in the generated form:

Property Effect sh:name Label shown for the field in the form (one per UI language, e.g. "Surname"@en, "Nachname"@de) sh:description Help text displayed below the field (one per UI language) sh:path The RDF property this field represents (e.g. schema:familyName) sh:minCount Minimum number of values; sh:minCount 1 makes the field required sh:maxCount Maximum number of values; sh:maxCount 1 restricts to a single value sh:datatype Datatype of the value (e.g. xsd:string, xsd:date, xsd:integer) sh:nodeKind sh:IRI Value must be an IRI (used for owl:sameAs and linked entity fields) sh:in Fixed list of allowed values for an enum / dropdown field sh:class Class of the linked entity (for cross-reference fields) sh:or Allows a field to accept alternative shapes (e.g. a single date or a date span) sh:pattern Regex the value must match (e.g. ^http(s)?://.+?/..+? for URL fields) sh:order Controls the order in which fields appear in the form sh:group Groups related fields under a shared heading

docs.title: Example: Person Shape
docs.text:
The following is a simplified excerpt from person.shacl:

@prefix sh:     <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#> .
@prefix melod:  <https://lod.academy/melod/vocab/ontology#> .
@prefix schema: <https://schema.org/> .
@prefix owl:    <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#> .
@prefix xsd:    <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> .
@prefix skos:   <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#> .
@prefix dataset: <https://adwmainz.pages.gitlab.rlp.net/nfdi4culture/cdmd/project_templates/mermeid-template/datasets/> .

melod:PersonShape
    a sh:NodeShape ;
    sh:targetClass melod:Person ;
    sh:property [
        sh:path schema:familyName ;
        sh:name "Surname"@en, "Nachname"@de ;
        sh:description "Surname of the person"@en, "Nachname der Person"@de ;
        sh:minCount 1 ;
        sh:maxCount 1 ;
        sh:datatype xsd:string ;
        sh:group melod:General ;
    ] ;
    sh:property [
        sh:path schema:givenName ;
        sh:name "First name"@en, "Vorname"@de ;
        sh:maxCount 1 ;
        sh:group melod:General ;
    ] ;
    sh:property [
        sh:path owl:sameAs ;
        sh:name "Link"@en, "Link"@de ;
        sh:description "Identifier e.g. GND, VIAF"@en, "Identifier z.B. GND, VIAF"@de ;
        sh:nodeKind sh:IRI ;
        sh:pattern "^http(s)?://.+?/..+?" ;
        sh:group melod:General ;
    ] ;
    sh:property [
        sh:path schema:gender ;
        sh:name "Gender"@en, "Geschlecht"@de ;
        sh:in ( "female" "male" "diverse" ) ;
        sh:maxCount 1 ;
        sh:group melod:General ;
    ] ;
    sh:property [
        sh:path schema:birthPlace ;
        sh:name "Place"@en, "Ort"@de ;
        sh:class melod:PlaceEntity ;
        sh:maxCount 1 ;
        sh:group melod:Birth ;
    ] ;
    sh:targetClass melod:Person .

melod:General a sh:PropertyGroup ;
    rdfs:label "General Information"@en, "Allgemeine Informationen"@de .
melod:Birth a sh:PropertyGroup ;
    rdfs:label "Birth"@en, "Geburt"@de .

docs.title: Multilingual Labels
docs.text: The editor supports the UI languages English (en) and German (de). The form receives the selected language via the data-language attribute and shows the labels that match it. Therefore all labels — sh:name, sh:description, the rdfs:label of property groups and of sh:or alternatives — should be given once per language with language tags (@en, @de).

docs.title: Linked Entity Fields
docs.text:
Fields that reference other entities (e.g. "Birth place" → Place) use sh:class to specify the type of the linked entity. The class is the index class of the target type, melod:<Type>Entity (e.g. melod:PlaceEntity, melod:PersonEntity, melod:ExpressionEntity), which is produced by the index queries (see Datasets Generation). The editor populates the dropdown for such fields from the repository's index files.

Fields that accept several entity types use sh:or:

sh:or (
    [ sh:class melod:PersonEntity ; rdfs:label "Person"@en, "Person"@de ]
    [ sh:class melod:InstitutionEntity ; rdfs:label "Institution"@en, "Institution"@de ]
) ;

docs.title: How Dropdowns Are Populated
docs.text:
When a form is opened, the editor fetches the SHACL shape and appends the content of all files in the repository's indexes/ folder to it. The combined Turtle is passed to shacl-form as a blob: URL. shacl-form then offers every entity typed with the requested class (e.g. melod:PlaceEntity) in the dropdown.

This allows the same SHACL shape files to work with any repository.

docs.title: Adding a New Field
docs.text:
To add a field to an existing entity type, open the corresponding .shacl file and add a new sh:property block to the node shape. For example, to add an "Honorific prefix" field to the Person shape:

sh:property [
    sh:path schema:honorificPrefix ;
    sh:name "Honorific prefix"@en, "Namenszusatz"@de ;
    sh:description "Title or honorific, e.g. Dr."@en, "Titel, z.B. Dr."@de ;
    sh:datatype xsd:string ;
    sh:group melod:General ;
] ;

Save the file and reload the editor — the new field will appear in all Person forms automatically.
