docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide covers everything you need to get from zero to your first saved entity in MerMEId MeLODy.

docs.title: Browser Recommendation
docs.text: MerMEId MeLODy runs entirely in the browser. Chromium-based browsers (Chrome or Edge) are recommended for the best experience. Firefox works for most operations, but the File System Access API (used for local filesystem mode) is not supported in Firefox.

docs.title: Git Host Account
docs.text: You need an account on a Git hosting platform to create data repositories — GitHub or GitLab (gitlab.com or a self-hosted GitLab instance such as GitLab RLP) are supported. The editor communicates directly with the GitHub or GitLab API; other Git hosts are not supported right now. To edit data in the repository you don't need a Git account, only the data owner needs one.

docs.title: Personal Access Token
docs.text:
The editor authenticates to your Git host using either a project-specific or a user-based personal access token (PAT). You need to create one or ask an admin to create one before adding a repository.

GitHub — creating a token user-based: (GitHub account required)

  1. Go to Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic).
  2. Click "Generate new token (classic)".
  3. Give it a descriptive name (e.g. mermeid-melody).
  4. Set an expiration date.
  5. Select the repo scope (full control of private repositories).
  6. Click "Generate token" and copy the result immediately — it is shown only once.

GitHub — creating a token project-specific: (for users without GitHub account, Organization required)

  1. Go to Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Fine-grained tokens.
  2. Click "Generate new token".
  3. Choose organization as resource owner
  4. Set Repository access to "Only select repositories" and choose project-specific repository
  5. Give it a descriptive name (e.g. mermeid-melody).
  6. Set an expiration date.
  7. Under Repository permissions, set Contents to "Read and write" (Metadata: Read-only is added automatically).
  8. Click "Generate token" and copy the result immediately — it is shown only once.

GitLab — creating a token user-based: (GitLab Account required)

  1. Go to your user Settings → Access Tokens.
  2. Click "Add new token".
  3. Select the scope api.
  4. Set an expiry date if required by your organisation.
  5. Click "Create personal access token" and copy the result immediately — it is shown only once.

GitLab — creating a token project-specific: (without GitLab account)

  1. Go to your repositories Settings → Access Tokens.
  2. Click "Add new token".
  3. Choose the role Maintainer (or higher) and select the scope api.
  4. Set an expiry date if required by your organisation.
  5. Click "Create project access token" and copy the result immediately — it is shown only once.

Store the token somewhere safe (e.g. a password manager).

docs.title: Creating a Data Repository
docs.text:
All metadata lives in a Git repository with a predefined folder structure. The quickest way to create one is to use the official template:

  1. Go to the MerMEId MeLODy Template on GitHub or to the GitLab MerMEId MeLODy Template.
  2. Click "Use this template" → "Create a new repository" (on GitLab: create a new project from the template or fork it).
  3. Choose an owner and give the repository a meaningful name (e.g. mozart-catalogue).
  4. Choose the visibility. The repository can be public or private.
  5. Click "Create repository".
  6. Make sure the CI/CD pipeline is allowed to push the generated indexes back to the repository:
    • GitHub: nothing to do — the workflow requests write access itself. If your organisation restricts workflow permissions, allow GitHub Actions to write to the repository (Settings → Actions → General).
    • GitLab: go to Settings → CI/CD → Job token permissions and allow Git push requests with the CI/CD job token (or adapt the push_indexes job to use a project access token).

The template includes the correct folder structure, sample data, the configuration file configuration/config.json, and a CI/CD pipeline that regenerates the search indexes in the indexes/ folder after every push to main. The SPARQL queries used to build the indexes are fetched from the editor repository during the pipeline run, so they always match the current editor version.

The editor itself also keeps the files in indexes/ up to date whenever you save, delete, or synchronise entities, so you can start working right away. The pipeline makes sure the indexes stay consistent when files are changed outside the editor.

The file configuration/config.json contains the IRI prefix domain for new entities (projectDomain). For more details see Repository Configuration.

The template contains a small amount of sample data you can delete once you are comfortable with the editor.

docs.title: Adding a Repository to the Editor
docs.text:
Once your data repository exists and you have a token, connect the editor to it:

  1. Open MerMEId MeLODy in your browser.
  2. In the left panel, click the "Add repository" button (folder-plus icon, top-left toolbar).
  3. Enter the repository folder name as display name — this is only used inside the editor (e.g. mozart-catalogue). It must start with a letter or digit and may only contain letters, digits, _, - and . (no spaces).
  4. Enter the repository URL — e.g. https://github.com/yourname/mozart-catalogue. The URL may end with .git or not; copying the address from the browser's address bar works as well. SSH URLs (git@github.com:...) are converted automatically.
  5. Enter your username (your GitHub or GitLab username, or choose one, if you don't have an account).
  6. Enter your personal access token.
  7. Click "Next" and select the branch you want to work on. If the repository has only one branch, or a branch named main, it is preselected.
  8. Decide whether to "Use lazy loading" (enabled by default). With lazy loading, only the list of files is downloaded and each file is fetched when you open it for the first time — recommended for large repositories. Turn it off to download all files at once.
  9. Click "Clone". A progress indicator is shown while the files are loaded.

The folder name, URL and username of the last added repository are prefilled the next time you open the dialog.

Once finished, the repository appears in the left panel and is selected automatically. Click on its name to select another repository — the name is highlighted when the repository is active.

When a repository is selected for the first time, the editor creates the catalog files dataCatalogs/catalog.ttl, dataCollections/works.ttl and dataCollections/manifestations.ttl if they are missing. They appear in the Share files section and can be shared like any other file.

docs.title: Adding a Local Folder
docs.text:
Instead of a remote URL, you can also work on a folder on your computer (Chromium-based browsers only). On the first page of the dialog, click the folder-plus button below "Or add a local folder instead" and choose the folder in the browser's folder picker. If the folder is not yet a Git repository, it is initialised. Optionally enter username and token so you can synchronise and share with the remote configured in the folder.

After a browser restart, the editor asks you again for permission to access the folder when you click the repository.

docs.title: Your First Entity
docs.text:
Once you have a repository selected:

  1. Click the "New" button in the editor toolbar to open the entity type dialog.
  2. Select an entity type (start with Person or Place — they have fewer required fields).
  3. A blank form opens in the main area. Fill in the required fields (marked with an asterisk).
  4. Click "Save" — the button becomes active and shows a dot indicator when there are unsaved changes. Saving is only possible when all required fields are filled and valid.
  5. In the bottom left corner you see Share files. Check all files you want to share, optionally enter a commit message, and click the Share files button.

The file is now saved to the Git repository, see Git Workflow for further information.

For a full description of all entity types and their fields, see Working with Entities and Data Model.

docs.title: Working with Entities
docs.text: This page covers the full lifecycle of an entity in MerMEId MeLODy — from creating a new record through filling in the form, linking to other entities, saving, undoing changes, and deleting.

docs.title: Creating a New Entity
docs.text:
1. Make sure a repository is selected (highlighted) in the left panel.
  2. Click the "New" button (file-plus icon) in the editor toolbar.
  3. A dialog opens listing all available entity types. Select the type you want to create (e.g. Person, Work, Place).
  4. Click "Create". The dialog closes and a blank form opens in the editor panel.

A new entity IRI is generated automatically at this point (see below). The entity does not exist as a file yet — it is only in memory until you save.

docs.title: Auto-Generated IRIs
docs.text:
Every entity gets a unique IRI when it is created. By default, IRIs use the urn:uuid: scheme and take the form:

urn:uuid:<folder>/<randomInteger>

For example, a new person entity might get the IRI urn:uuid:persons/2847362910.

The prefix can be changed with projectDomain in configuration/config.json, and an optional IDprefix per folder can be placed in front of the number (e.g. urn:uuid:works/w1477695404). See Repository Configuration.

The IRI is displayed below the toolbar in the editor panel and cannot be changed after creation.

docs.title: Filling in the Form
docs.text: The form is generated automatically from the SHACL shape for the entity type. Different field types appear depending on the property being described. Field labels and help texts are shown in the language selected in the header (English or German).

docs.title: Field Types
docs.text:
Text fields — plain literal values. Type directly into the input. Most label and name fields are text fields (e.g. Surname, First name, title).

Rich text fields — some description fields offer a rich text editor with basic formatting. The content is stored as HTML.

IRI / Link fields — expect a full IRI (URL) as value. The field may validate that the entered value matches the expected IRI pattern. For example, the owl:sameAs field ("Link") on a Person expects a value like http://d-nb.info/gnd/118816X. An error is shown if the value does not match the required pattern ^http(s)?://.+?/..+?.

Dropdown / enum fields — a fixed list of allowed values to choose from. For example, the Gender field on a Person offers female, male, and diverse. Click the dropdown to see the options.

Date fields — some date fields offer a choice between a single date and a date span (a start and end date or not before, not after). A dropdown lets you switch between the two modes. Dates are entered in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

Linked entity reference fields — allow you to select another entity from the dataset (e.g. a Birth Place linking to a Place entity). These are described in detail in the next section.

docs.title: Required Fields
docs.text: Fields marked with an asterisk (*) or highlighted as required must be filled before the entity can be saved. If a required field is empty or a value is invalid, saving is blocked and the message "Cannot save entity. Please fill out all required fields or correct invalid fields." is shown.

docs.title: Linking Entities
docs.text: Many fields reference other entities — for example, a Person has a Birth Place (linking to a Place entity), and a Work has a Contributor (linking to a Person entity). These cross-references are what make the data model a true Linked Open Data graph.

docs.title: How Cross-References Work
docs.text:
Linked entity fields appear as dropdown menus populated from the index files in the indexes/ folder of the selected repository. When you click on a linked entity field, a searchable list of existing entities of the appropriate type appears.

Select the entity you want to link. The IRI of the selected entity is written into the Turtle file as the value of the property.

docs.title: Quick Add
docs.text:
If the entity you want to link does not exist yet, you do not need to leave the current form to create it. The Quick Add feature lets you create a new linked entity inline:

  1. In the linked entity field, look for the "Quick Add" button (the + button next to the field).
  2. Click it. A Quick Add dialog opens with a form for the linked entity type (e.g. a Place form if you are filling in a Birth Place).
  3. Fill in the required fields and click "Save" in the Quick Add dialog. The button is enabled once the form is valid; Cancel closes the dialog without saving.
  4. The new entity is saved, staged and added to the index, and it is selected automatically in the field from which you opened the dialog.
  5. Save the main form to keep the link.

The Quick Add entity is staged for git in the same way as a manually saved entity — it will appear in the Share Files section and must be shared to become available to other users.

docs.title: Previewing Linked Entities
docs.text:
While editing, you can inspect any linked entity without leaving the current form:

  1. In the form, find a field that shows a linked entity value (displayed as a clickable link).
  2. Click the link.
  3. A floating side panel opens. It shows a read-only rendering of the linked entity using a second shacl-form in data-view mode. You can move the panel by dragging its header and resize it.
  4. At the top of the side panel, an "Edit" button opens the linked entity in the main editor (replacing the currently open form). Use with care if you have unsaved changes in the current form — you will be warned before switching.

The preview panel can also be opened from the Graph tab. It is useful for quickly checking the details of a linked entity without navigating away from your work.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text: Click the "Save" button (floppy-disk icon) to save the current entity.

docs.title: Unsaved Changes Indicator
docs.text: As soon as you make any change to the form, the Save button becomes active and shows a dot indicator. This visual cue reminds you that the current state has not been saved yet.

docs.title: What Happens When You Save
docs.text:
1. The shacl-form serialises the current form state as RDF/Turtle.
  2. The Turtle content is written to the corresponding .ttl file in the browser's storage.
  3. The file is staged for sharing.
  4. The index file of the entity type in indexes/ is updated and the search is reloaded. The updated index file is staged as well and is shared together with your data.
  5. The file appears in the Share Files section in the repository panel.

New works and manifestations are automatically added to the repository's default data collection ("All works" or "All manifestations").

Saving does not push anything to the remote Git repository. The data is stored only in the browser until you explicitly share (push) the file.

docs.title: Undoing Changes
docs.text:
Click the "Undo" button (arrow-counterclockwise icon) in the entity editor toolbar to discard your unsaved changes.

Undo resets the form to the state in which the entity was loaded into the editor. It does not unstage the file if it had already been staged — use the Unstage button in the Share Files section for that.

docs.title: Deleting an Entity
docs.text:
1. Open the entity you want to delete by clicking on its file in the repository tree.
  2. Click the red "Delete" button (file-minus icon) in the entity editor toolbar or the "Remove entity" button (file-minus icon) in the repositories section (left side).
  3. A Confirm deletion dialog appears asking "Do you really want to delete this entity?". Click "Delete" to confirm or "Cancel" to abort.
  4. The file is removed from the repository tree, its entry is removed from the index, and the editor is cleared.
  5. If the file already existed in the remote repository, the deleted file appears in the Share Files section with a -deleted suffix in its filename (e.g. persons/2847362910.ttl-deleted). A new file that was never shared is simply removed.
  6. To push the deletion to the remote repository, check the box next to the deleted file entry and click "Share files".

If you change your mind before pushing, use the Unstage files button in the Share Files section to restore the file to the last synchronised state.

Note: deleting an entity locally and pushing the deletion removes the file from the Git repository. Any other entities that linked to the deleted entity will retain the IRI reference but it will no longer resolve to a file.

docs.title: Git Workflow
docs.text: MerMEId MeLODy uses a Git repository on GitHub or GitLab to store and synchronise your data. This page explains how the Git integration works and how to manage your repositories effectively.

docs.title: How Storage Works
docs.text:
MerMEId MeLODy stores all data in a virtual filesystem running inside your browser. This virtual filesystem is persisted in the browser's Origin Private File System (OPFS) — a private storage area of the browser that survives page refreshes and browser restarts. Alternatively, you can work directly on a local folder on your computer.

The editor communicates directly with the GitHub or GitLab API to download files and to create commits. Every operation (adding, synchronising, sharing) is executed entirely in the browser.

docs.title: Credentials Storage
docs.text:
Your repository folder name, repository url and git username are stored in the browser's local storage.

These values are written to the local storage during the clone operation and read back before adding a new repository. They persist across browser sessions (as long as you do not clear the browser storage). They are not sent anywhere except to your Git host during authenticated requests.

docs.title: Adding a Repository
docs.text:
Adding a repository in MerMEId MeLODy is equivalent to git clone. Here is what happens step by step:

  1. Open the "Add repository" dialog (folder-plus icon in the repository panel toolbar).
  2. Enter the display name, repository URL, and — if required — username and personal access token.
  3. Click "Next".
  4. Select a branch (usually main), decide whether to use lazy loading, and click "Clone".
  5. The editor downloads the files via the API:
    • With lazy loading (default), only the list of files is downloaded. Each file is fetched the first time you open it. This keeps adding a repository fast even for large repositories.
    • Without lazy loading, all files are downloaded at once.
  6. Credentials are stored in the browser's local storage.
  7. The repository appears in the left panel. Click its name to select it.

docs.title: Selecting a Repository
docs.text:
Click the repository name (the top-level node in the tree) to select it. The name is highlighted when the repository is active. Only one repository can be active at a time. All entity creation, editing, and saving operations apply to the currently selected repository.

When the page is loaded, the first repository is selected automatically for the search.

docs.title: Sharing Changes
docs.text: "Sharing" files means committing and pushing them to the remote Git repository. This is equivalent to git commit + git push.

docs.title: Staging Queue
docs.text: Every time you save an entity, the file is added to the Share Files staging queue at the bottom of the repository panel. The queue shows all files that have been modified locally but not yet pushed.

docs.title: Selective Commit
docs.text:
You do not have to push all staged files at once. The staging queue allows selective commit:

  1. In the Share Files section, check the boxes next to the files you want to include in this push (or use Select all).
  2. Optionally enter a commit message. Otherwise the current date and your username are used.
  3. Click the "Share files" button (cloud-upload icon).
  4. The editor checks whether the selected files have been changed online in the meantime (see Conflict Check below).
  5. A commit is created containing only the checked files, and pushed to the remote.

Files that were not checked remain in the staging queue for a future push.

docs.title: Conflict Check Before Sharing
docs.text:
Before committing and pushing, MerMEId MeLODy compares each selected file with its current version in the remote repository:

  • If none of the selected files have been changed online since your last synchronisation, the files are shared immediately.
  • If one or more files have been changed online (or deleted online), the Sharing conflicts dialog opens.

The Sharing conflicts dialog lists every affected file and shows your version ("Your version (not yet shared)") next to the current online version, with the differences highlighted. For each file you choose one option:

  • Keep my version (or Delete file, if you deleted it locally) — your version is shared and overwrites the online version.
  • Use online version — your local changes are discarded and the online version is loaded. Nothing is shared for this file.
  • Decide later — the file is skipped for now and stays in the staging queue.

If several files are affected, the buttons All: Keep my version and All: Use online version apply the choice to all of them. Once a decision has been made for every file, click Apply and share. Cancel aborts sharing.

New files that do not exist online yet never cause a conflict.

docs.title: Synchronising
docs.text: "Synchronising" means downloading the latest changes from the remote repository. This is similar to git pull.

docs.title: How to Synchronise
docs.text: Click the "Synchronize repository" button (cloud-download icon) in the repository panel toolbar. A personal access token is required for synchronising; if the repository has none, add one in the Repository settings.

docs.title: What Happens During Synchronisation
docs.text:
1. The editor downloads all files that have been changed online since the last synchronisation and removes files that have been deleted online.
  2. Your staged (not yet shared) files are kept and re-applied afterwards, so you don't lose any local work.
  3. The index files are updated for the changed files and the repository tree is refreshed.

Synchronising does not check for conflicts. If a staged file has also been changed online, the differences are resolved the next time you share the file (see Conflict Check Before Sharing).

docs.title: Unsaved Changes Warning
docs.text: If you have unsaved changes in the editor (the Save button is blue), you will be warned before synchronising. Save or discard the current changes first.

docs.title: Unstaging Files
docs.text:
To discard local saved changes for a specific file and restore it to the last synchronised state:

  1. In the Share Files section, check the box next to the file you want to unstage.
  2. Click the "Unstage files" button (arrow-counterclockwise icon).
  3. The file is removed from the Share Files queue and the local copy is restored to the version from your last synchronisation. A new file that was never shared is removed completely. The index and the open form are updated accordingly.

This is equivalent to git restore --staged <file> && git restore <file> in standard Git.

docs.title: Removing a Repository
docs.text:
Click the "Remove repository" button (folder-minus icon) in the repository panel toolbar. The repository is removed immediately from the browser's storage — there is no confirmation dialog, so make sure you have shared all changes you want to keep. For local folders, only the reference in the editor is removed; the files on your disk are not touched.

Important: removing a repository from the editor does not delete anything on the remote. The Git repository on GitHub or GitLab is completely unaffected. You can re-add it at any time using the Add Repository dialog.

docs.title: Renaming a Repository
docs.text: Click the "Rename repository" button (folder icon) in the repository panel toolbar. Enter a new display name. This only changes the label shown in the editor — it does not rename the remote repository or affect anything in the Git history.

docs.title: Git Command Reference
docs.text:
For users familiar with Git, the following table maps MerMEId MeLODy operations to their standard Git equivalents:

MerMEId MeLODy operation Git equivalent Notes Add repository git clone --depth 1 --single-branch Files are downloaded via the API (lazy or all at once); no Git history Synchronise git pull Downloads changed files via the API; staged local files are kept Save write file + git add Local only, no network; also updates the index files Share files git commit + git push Selective — only checked files; conflict check per file; one commit via the GitHub/GitLab API Unstage files git restore --staged + git restore Restores the last synchronised version Remove repository rm -rf <repo> (local only) Remote is unaffected

docs.title: The Interface
docs.text: This page gives a complete walkthrough of the MerMEId MeLODy user interface. The editor is divided into three main areas: a left panel with search and file navigation, a central editing area, and a right output panel.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  BETA          MerMEId MeLODy        [Language: EN] [Docs] [GitHub] │
├─────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────┤
│ Search Panel    │  Editor Panel                 │  Output Panel     │
│                 │                               │                   │
│ Entity Search   │  Entity Editor                │  XML | RDF |      │
│                 │                               │  Preview | Graph  │
│                 │  [toolbar]                    │                   │
│                 │  Entity type + IRI            │                   │
│                 │  shacl-form                   │                   │
│ Repository      │                               │                   │
│ Panel           │                               │                   │
│                 │                               │                   │
│ Filesystem      │                               │                   │
│ Manager         │                               │                   │
│                 │                               │                   │
│                 │                               │                   │
├─────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┴───────────────────┤
│  Footer                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

The header shows the CDMD logo with the BETA badge (click it to read a popup with the beta disclaimer and contact information), the application title, and three buttons:

  • Language — switches the user interface between English and German (Language: EN / Language: DE). The selected language is used for buttons, entity type names and the labels in the forms. Some dialogs and messages are currently only available in English. The selection is not remembered after reloading the page.
  • Docs — opens this documentation.
  • GitHub — opens the source code repository of the editor.

The footer shows the logos of the funding and partner institutions: DFG, CDMD, ZenMEM, and ADW Mainz.

docs.title: The Search Panel
docs.text:
Component: Entity Search (top of the left column)

The search panel let you find entities across the entire dataset without navigating through the file tree. You can search by names, titles, composers, alternative titles, or classifications.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
• Type filter dropdown — narrows your search to a specific entity type (Person, Place, Work, Institution, Data Collection, etc.). Select All to search across all entity types.
  • Search input field — type a name, keyword, or phrase to find matching entities. The search is case-insensitive and looks across multiple fields:
  • Primary labels — the main name or title of an entity
  • Alternative labels — alternate names or spellings registered for an entity (e.g., if "J.S. Bach" and "Johann Sebastian Bach" are both registered) or alternative/uniform titles
  • Classifications — broader categories an entity belongs to
  • Results list — shows matching entities with a label indicating their type. Click any result to open it in the editor. The file tree on the left will automatically navigate to that file.

docs.title: How the Search Index Works
docs.text:
• Start with a partial name — you don't need to type the full name; "Bach" will find all Bachs, "Sonata" will find all sonatas
  • Use type filters — if you're looking for a specific person but the name is common, first filter by Person, then search
  • Look for alternative spellings — if you can't find an entity by its common name, the search may know it by another spelling

docs.title: Important Note About Search Results
docs.text:
The search reads the index files in the indexes/ folder of the selected repository. The editor updates these index files itself whenever you save, delete or unstage an entity, and when you synchronise. This means:

  • Entities you have just created or edited appear in the search results immediately after saving, even before you share them.
  • Changes made by other people appear after you synchronize the repository.
  • To reload the search indexes manually, use the Reload indexes button (arrow-clockwise icon, far left in the editor toolbar).

docs.title: The Repository Panel
docs.text:
Component: Filesystem Manager (below the search panel, left side)

The repository panel shows your cloned repositories, their folder structure, and the file staging area.

docs.title: Toolbar Buttons
docs.text:
Icon Action Description Folder-plus Add repository Opens the dialog to connect a new Git repository or a local folder Folder-minus Remove repository Removes the repository from the browser's storage (does not delete the remote) Folder Rename repository Renames the display name shown in the editor (does not affect the remote) Cloud-download Synchronize repository Downloads the latest changes from the remote repository File-minus Remove entity Deletes the entity file selected in the tree Gear Repository settings Changes the username and personal access token stored for the repository Journal-bookmark Catalog metadata Opens the metadata form of the repository's data catalog

These buttons operate on whichever repository is currently selected (highlighted in the tree). They are enabled once you have clicked or expanded a repository. Synchronize repository is disabled for local folders without a configured remote.

docs.title: The Repository Settings Dialog
docs.text: Opens a dialog with the username and personal access token used for the selected repository. Use it to add a token to a repository that was added without one, or to replace an expired token. Click Save to store the new values.

docs.title: The Catalog Metadata Dialog
docs.text: Each repository contains one data catalog (dataCatalogs/catalog.ttl) that describes the catalogue as a whole — its name, contributors with their roles, and a description. The dialog shows the catalog in a form; Save is enabled once the form is valid. Saving stages the file in the Share Files section.

docs.title: The Repository Tree
docs.text:
Each repository is shown as a collapsible tree. Click the arrow next to a folder to expand it. The tree is lazy-loaded — folder contents are read from the browser's storage only when you expand a node.

Each tree node is one of:

  • Repository root (top level) — click to select the repository; the name highlights to confirm it is active
  • Folder (e.g. persons/, works/) — expand to see the files inside
  • File (e.g. 12345.ttl) — click to open in the editor

Files that have been modified and saved (staged) are visually indicated in the tree so you can see which records have pending changes.

docs.title: The Share Files Section
docs.text:
At the bottom of the repository panel is the Share files section. This lists all files that have been saved locally but not yet pushed to the remote repository.

  • Each staged file is listed with its path (e.g. persons/2847362910.ttl) and a checkbox next to it. Click the file name to open it in the editor.
  • Check the boxes for the files you want to include in the next commit, or use the Select all button (check-square icon) to select or deselect all files.
  • Optionally enter a Commit-Message. If you leave it empty, the date and your username are used.
  • Click the "Share files" button (cloud-upload icon) to commit and push the selected files. The button is enabled once at least one file is selected.
  • Click the "Unstage files" button (arrow-counterclockwise icon) to discard local changes and restore the files to the last synchronised state.

Deleted entities also appear here with a -deleted suffix in the filename, if the file already existed in the remote repository.

docs.title: The Editor Panel
docs.text:
Component: Entity Editor (centre column)

The editor panel is the main working area. It displays the form for the currently open entity.

docs.title: Toolbar Buttons
docs.text: Icon Action Description Arrow-clockwise Reload indexes Reloads the search and dropdown indexes from the repository's indexes/ folder File-plus New Opens the entity type dialog to create a new entity Floppy disk Save Saves the current entity to the browser's storage and stages it for sharing File-minus Delete Deletes the current entity (prompts for confirmation) Arrow-counterclockwise Undo Discards all unsaved changes and resets the form to the state in which the entity was loaded

docs.title: Entity Type and IRI Display
docs.text:
Below the toolbar, the editor shows:

  • The entity type (e.g. Person, Work) as a label
  • The entity IRI — the unique identifier for this entity (e.g. urn:uuid:persons/2847362910)

These are read-only and generated automatically when a new entity is created.

docs.title: The Form (shacl-form)
docs.text:
The form is rendered by the shacl-form web component (in the MerMEId-specific version mermeid-shacl-form). It is generated automatically from the SHACL shape file for the entity type. Each field in the form corresponds to an RDF property defined in the SHACL shape.

See Working with Entities for a detailed description of how to fill in the form.

docs.title: Unsaved Changes Indicator
docs.text: When you make any change to the form, the Save button turns blue and a dot indicator appears on or near the button. This is a reminder that the current state has not been written to the virtual filesystem yet. Clicking a different file in the tree without saving will trigger a warning.

docs.title: The Output Panel
docs.text:
Component: Entity Renderer (right column, tab group)

The output panel on the right side of the screen renders the current entity's data in different formats. The XML, RDF and Preview tabs update when an entity is opened or saved, not while you are typing. The Preview tab is shown by default.

docs.title: XML Tab
docs.text:
Shows the entity data converted from JSON-LD to MEI/XML or TEI/XML format. This conversion is performed by entity-type-specific converter modules. The output is suitable for copying into MEI or TEI documents or passing to MEI-aware tools.

A copy button at the top of the tab copies the full XML content to the clipboard.

docs.title: RDF Tab
docs.text:
Shows the RDF/Turtle output — the exact content that is inside the .ttl file. This is produced directly by shacl-form.serialize() and represents the canonical stored format for the entity.

A copy button at the top of the tab copies the Turtle content to the clipboard.

docs.title: Preview Tab
docs.text: Shows a read-only rendering of the current entity using a second shacl-form instance in data-view mode. This gives a cleaner, label-based view of the data without the editable input controls. It is useful for reviewing entries before pushing.

docs.title: Graph Tab
docs.text:
Shows the related entities of the current entity as an interactive graph. The relations are taken from the repository's indexes, so entities linking to the current entity are shown as well as entities it links to.

  • Nodes are coloured by entity type; a legend and a type filter ("Related: All / …") let you restrict the view to one type.
  • Click a node to expand its own relations. If an entity has many relations, only the first ones are shown together with a "+N more" node.
  • Use the zoom buttons to zoom in, zoom out or reset the view, and switch between the graph and a list view.
  • The eye icon on a node opens the entity in the floating preview panel (see Previewing Linked Entities).

docs.title: Mobile Layout
docs.text:
On small screens, the three-panel layout collapses. A toggle button allows switching between the left panel and the main editing area. The output panel may require scrolling or is hidden depending on screen width.

For the best experience on small screens, use landscape orientation. Full multi-panel layout requires a screen width of more than 900px.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
This page covers the most common problems encountered when using MerMEId MeLODy and explains how to resolve them.

For detailed error information, open your browser's developer console (press F12 or Ctrl+Shift+I, then go to the Console tab). Error messages from the GitHub/GitLab API and from the editor's own modules appear there and are usually descriptive enough to pinpoint the cause.

docs.title: Clone Fails / No Branches Listed
docs.text:
Symptom: Clicking "Next" in the Add Repository dialog shows no branches, or displays an error such as "Failed to load branches. Please check the repository URL, username and personal access token, then press "Next" again." or "The repository URL is not valid."

Possible causes and solutions:

  • Wrong URL format. The repository URL must point to a repository on GitHub or GitLab, e.g. https://github.com/yourname/my-catalogue or https://gitlab.com/group/subgroup/my-catalogue. The .git ending is optional, and SSH URLs (git@...) are converted automatically. Other Git hosts are not supported.

  • Wrong token scope. Your personal access token must have permission to access the repository via the API. On GitHub, this means the repo scope (classic token) or Contents: Read and write (fine-grained token). On GitLab, this means the api scope. Tokens with only read_repository/write_repository, package or CI scopes will not work. Generate a new token with the correct scope if needed.

  • Repository is empty. A newly created repository that contains no commits cannot be cloned. GitHub and GitLab show an empty state page when you visit a repository with no commits. To resolve this, initialize the repository — the easiest way is to create it from the MerMEId MeLODy Template, which already contains an initial commit.

  • API rate limit. GitHub limits the number of API requests without a token, and self-hosted GitLab instances may reject too many requests (HTTP 429). The editor retries automatically; if the error persists, wait a few minutes and always use a personal access token.

docs.title: Sharing Fails
docs.text:
Symptom: Clicking "Share files" fails with the message "Failed to share files with remote repository. Try to synchronize before sharing."

Possible causes: The personal access token has expired or lacks write permission, or the branch has been changed online in a way that prevents the commit.

Solution:

  1. Check the token in the Repository settings (gear icon) and replace it if necessary.
  2. Click "Synchronize repository" (cloud-download icon) to download the latest changes.
  3. Once the synchronisation completes successfully, try "Share files" again.

docs.title: Sharing Conflicts
docs.text:
Symptom: The Sharing conflicts dialog appears listing files that have been changed both locally and online.

Cause: The same file was modified both in your local staged changes and in a remote commit since your last synchronisation. MerMEId MeLODy detects this before sharing to prevent data loss.

Solution:

  • Decide for each file whether to keep your version, use the online version, or decide later, then click Apply and share. See Conflict Check Before Sharing for details. You don't need to unstage the files first.

docs.title: Form Is Empty After Opening a File
docs.text:
Symptom: Clicking a .ttl file in the repository tree opens the editor panel but the form shows no fields or no data, or a message like "The selected document needs one statement with entity IRI and entity type!" or "The selected file is empty or does not exist anymore." appears.

Possible causes:

  • The file contains malformed Turtle. If a .ttl file was edited outside the editor and contains syntax errors, shacl-form may fail to parse it and render an empty form. Check the browser console for parsing errors. Correct the file in a text editor or ask an admin.
  • The file has no or more than one typed entity. Each file must contain exactly one subject with a urn:uuid: IRI and a melod: type.
  • The SHACL shape could not be loaded. If the shacl_file_location for the entity type is a URL that cannot be fetched (e.g. a wrong path or a 404), the form will be empty. Check the path in configuration/editor-default.ttl of the editor (not of the data repository).

docs.title: Search Returns No Results
docs.text:
Symptom: Typing in the search panel returns no results, even for entities you know exist.

Possible causes and solutions:

  • The indexes/ folder is missing or empty. The search reads the index files from the indexes/ folder of your repository. These files are generated by the CI/CD pipeline after each push to main and are updated by the editor whenever you save an entity. If the repository has no index files yet, they are created the first time you save an entity of each type. For details on how indexes are built, see Datasets Generation.

  • Need to reload. Click the "Reload indexes" button (arrow-clockwise icon in the editor toolbar) or reload the browser page.

  • No repository is selected. If no repository is active (nothing is highlighted in the repository tree), the search panel does not know which indexes to use. Click your repository name to select it.

docs.title: Editor Loads But No Repositories Are Shown
docs.text:
Symptom: The left panel is empty on first visit.

This is expected behaviour. MerMEId MeLODy stores everything in the browser's private storage (Origin Private File System). On a fresh browser profile (or after clearing browser data), there are no repositories yet. Use the "Add repository" button (folder-plus icon) to connect your first repository.

For local folders, the browser asks again for permission to access the folder after a restart. Click the repository and allow access. If access is not granted, the warning "Access to the local folder … was not granted." is shown.

docs.title: Changes of Others Not Visible in Search
docs.text:
Symptom: Other users pushed new or updated entities, but they do not appear in your search results.

Cause: Your local copy of the repository — including the indexes/ folder — only changes when you synchronise. In addition, the CI/CD pipeline on your Git host (GitHub Actions or GitLab CI) regenerates the index files after each push to main, which takes some time — typically 30 seconds to a few minutes.

Solution: Click "Synchronize repository" to download the latest files and indexes. If the indexes are still outdated, wait for the pipeline to finish. You can monitor its progress on GitHub (Actions tab) or GitLab (Build → Pipelines), then synchronise again.

Your own saved changes are visible in the search immediately, without sharing.

docs.title: Synchronising Is Not Possible
docs.text:
Symptom: The message "No personal access token. Synchronizing is not possible." appears, or the Synchronize repository or Share files buttons are disabled.

Solution:

  • Add a personal access token in the Repository settings (gear icon).
  • For local folders: synchronising and sharing require a remote repository configured in the folder's .git/config.
  • Share files is enabled only when at least one file is checked.
  • Try to select the repository first.

docs.title: Browser Compatibility Issues
docs.text:
Symptom: A feature does not work as expected in a particular browser.

Recommendation: Use Chrome or Edge (any recent Chromium-based version) for the best experience. Both support all features used by MerMEId MeLODy, including the Origin Private File System, the File System Access API, and the Web Crypto API.

Firefox works for most operations (adding repositories, editing, saving, sharing, synchronising, searching) but does not support the File System Access API. The local folder mode (direct access to a folder on your disk) is not available in Firefox.

Safari is not officially tested. Some features may not work.

docs.title: General Tip: Use the Browser Console
docs.text:
Most errors in MerMEId MeLODy produce a message in the browser's developer console. To open it:

  • Chrome / Edge: press F12 or Ctrl+Shift+I, then click the Console tab.
  • Firefox: press F12 or Ctrl+Shift+I, then click the Console tab.

Look for red error messages. API errors in particular are descriptive (e.g. GitHub API error: 401 or GitLab API error: 401 if your token is wrong or expired, 403 if it lacks permissions, or 404 if the repository URL is wrong). Copy the error message when reporting a bug on GitHub Issues.
